Error.description: Structured error envelope. Every non-2xx response uses this shape.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (e.g. ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND).

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Safe to surface to an end user.

retry_hint.description: How to retry, when retrying may help.

delay_ms.description: Suggested wait before retry, in milliseconds.

user_fixable.description: True when the caller can resolve this by changing the request.

retry_likely_to_succeed.description: True when an identical retry is likely to succeed.

row.description: Present on a PLATFORM_RATE_LIMIT raised because one account-safety budget row is paused: LinkedIn refused a recent call on that row, so this one was refused locally without reaching LinkedIn. Names the paused row (for example profile_views, connection_requests_no_note). The pause is scoped to this row on this account; every other row keeps working. Absent on every other rate limit. Also present on BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, where it names the row that hit its CEILING rather than one LinkedIn paused: read the code to tell the two apart, because the recovery differs. Null on a BUDGET_EXHAUSTED whose reason is activity_window and whose action spends no budget of its own, because there is no row to name; hint.parameter still names the setting to change (active_hours). Never null on a rate limit.

reset_at.description: Present on BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: the instant the refusal lifts, as an absolute instant rather than a duration, so it stays true however long you hold it. It is the window roll on a ceiling refusal and the next window open on an activity-window one. It is null in the two cases where no clock frees the account: the pending_invites gauge, whose backlog falls when invitations are accepted or withdrawn, and an InMail credit exhaustion (row inmail, hint.parameter inmail_credits), which LinkedIn regrants on a schedule this product cannot read.

hint.description: Present on BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: the exact setting to change, as a field rather than as prose. Limits are always enforced: to send more, raise the limit. parameter is addressable on PATCH /v1/{account_id}/safety-policy (update_safety_policy in MCP), so an agent can decide between waiting until reset_at, escalating to a human, and raising the limit, without parsing the message. The one exception is inmail_credits: not a policy field, LinkedIn's own InMail balance. Wait for LinkedIn to regrant credits, or buy more on LinkedIn.

parameter.description: The setting to change, for example profile_views.ceiling, active_hours (the account's or the Team's; the message names which), rows[posts].activity_window_end, profiles[basic].rows[posts].activity_window_start on the Team policy, or inmail_credits (LinkedIn's own balance, not a policy field).

message.description: One paragraph naming the limit, the ceiling, when it resets and how to raise it.

reason.description: Present on CONTACT_NOT_ENROLLABLE: why the Contact was not enrolled (already_enrolled, do_not_contact, in_exclusion_list, in_other_motion or filtered_out). Present on BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: which rule refused. ceiling means the row's configured limit is spent, and you wait until reset_at or raise it. activity_window means the account is outside the hours it works in, and reset_at is when the window next opens. The two need different fixes, so branch on this rather than on the message; hint.parameter already names the right setting for each.

blocked.description: Present on BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, always true: the action did not happen and spent nothing. Limits are always enforced; no success response carries a safety warning.

merged_into.description: Present on RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND for a Contact id that was merged into another Contact (two records turned out to be one person): the id to use instead.

retry_after.description: Present alongside row: whole seconds until that row is usable again. This response carries no Retry-After header and no delay retry_hint, deliberately: a paused row can be paused for an hour, and a client that sleeps that inside the call hangs. Do not retry this row before the wait elapses; switch to other work instead. Seconds, not milliseconds.

errors.description: Present on SEQUENCE_INVALID: every failure of the refused Sequence document, not only the first (the first 100; the message counts them all), in step order, so one fix round covers them all, each compiler-style with code, message, pointer, hint and docs_url. Also on WEBHOOK_TEMPLATE_INVALID: every finding of the refused body_template, in template order, in the same shape plus line and col. Also on MOTION_NOT_STARTABLE: every gap that keeps the Motion from starting, as path and rule only. path is relative to the document (for example opener.variants.opener_named.text or invite.with.withdraw_after); rule says what to change. The message repeats the first entry.

path.description: Where in the Sequence document: step id, then field. On WEBHOOK_TEMPLATE_INVALID: always body_template.

rule.description: The broken rule, phrased as the fix.

code.description: On SEQUENCE_INVALID: the rule id, R1 to R29. On WEBHOOK_TEMPLATE_INVALID: the rule id, T1 to T10.

message.description: On SEQUENCE_INVALID and WEBHOOK_TEMPLATE_INVALID: equal to rule.

pointer.description: On SEQUENCE_INVALID: an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the document you sent (for example /steps/5/with/withdraw_after), so a tool finds the line without parsing path. A missing key points at the object that lacks it. On WEBHOOK_TEMPLATE_INVALID: /body_template; line and col place the finding inside it.

hint.description: On SEQUENCE_INVALID and WEBHOOK_TEMPLATE_INVALID: one sentence saying what to do.

docs_url.description: On SEQUENCE_INVALID: the rule's entry on the Sequence rules page. On WEBHOOK_TEMPLATE_INVALID: the rule's entry on the body templates page.

severity.description: On SEQUENCE_INVALID and WEBHOOK_TEMPLATE_INVALID: always error here, an entry that refuses the document. Warnings never refuse; they come back in warnings[] on the success response.

candidates.description: On SEQUENCE_INVALID and WEBHOOK_TEMPLATE_INVALID, when there are some: did-you-mean replacements, best first.

line.description: On WEBHOOK_TEMPLATE_INVALID: the line in the body_template where the finding starts, counting from 1.

col.description: On WEBHOOK_TEMPLATE_INVALID: the column in that line, counting from 1.

current.description: Present on SEQUENCE_CONFLICT: the Motion's stored Sequence your PATCH was refused against, so you can merge or overwrite without a second read. To replace it with yours, send the PATCH again with if_sequence_revision set to current.sequence_revision.

sequence_version.description: The stored Sequence version.

sequence.description: The stored Sequence document, or null.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601: when the Motion last changed.

unresolved.description: Present when a structured search filter value matched several filter options and one has to be picked (422 FILTER_CANDIDATES_REQUIRED). One entry per offending value, so a single retry can fix them all. A value that matched no option at all is not listed here and is not an error: it is sent on as an id and reported in notices[] on the 200.

field.description: The request body field the value came from. Dotted for nested filters, for example author.company.

value.description: The value exactly as you sent it.

candidates.description: The filter options this value matched. Pick one and re-send its id.

id.description: The filter id to send instead of the display name.

portal_url.description: Present on PAYMENT_REQUIRED and ACCOUNT_DISPUTED: the self-service page where the tenant resolves the payment problem, so an agent can hand a human one link. Null when no portal session could be opened; fall back to the dashboard.

feature.description: Present on TIER_REQUIRED: the feature the team's Tier does not include (drafts, contacts, motions, network, unibox or keep_connected).

required_tier.description: Present on TIER_REQUIRED: the lowest Tier that includes the feature. Null when no Tier includes it.

current_tier.description: Present on TIER_REQUIRED: the team's Tier now, or the refused account's Tier when details.account_id is set. Null when there is none.

upgrade_url.description: Present on TIER_REQUIRED for a team Owner only: the dashboard page where the Tier is changed. Any other role gets none and asks an Owner.

attempts_remaining.description: Present on CHECKPOINT_INVALID_CODE: how many more verification codes the checkpoint accepts before it locks. Stop and ask the account owner for a fresh code when it reaches zero, rather than guessing.

challenge_type.description: Present on CHECKPOINT_UNSUPPORTED: the kind of verification challenge LinkedIn raised that cannot be solved through this API. A human has to complete it in LinkedIn, then the account reconnects.

account_id.description: Present on ACCOUNT_ALREADY_LINKED: the id of your own existing account for this LinkedIn profile, so you can reuse it instead of linking again. Only ever an account of the calling tenant.

connection_location.description: Present on CONNECTION_LOCATION_UNAVAILABLE after a location PATCH that did not land where asked: where the account connects from now (country, current_country, mode, strict), re-read after the change.

current_country.description: Country of the connection in use now.

mode.description: auto: Curviate proxy. custom: your own proxy.

strict.description: true: never connects from another country.

details.description: Present on INVALID_REQUEST, CONNECTION_LOCATION_REQUIRED and PLATFORM_ERROR when an account PATCH's location change was refused (your own proxy, a country, clearing the proxy): account says where the account stands now, re-read after the attempt. Never any proxy field. Present on EXPORT_IN_PROGRESS: export_id names the export your team already has queued or running. It may be a teammate's, which GET /v1/exports/{id} answers 404; it finishes or fails within the hour, then start yours. Present on INVALID_REQUEST when a safety-policy write sent a removed key: removed_key names it. Drop that key from the request; limits are always enforced. Present on TIER_REQUIRED when one account lacks the feature while the team has it (an account on a seat another team lent this one carries that seat's Tier): account_id names it. Leave that account out, or ask the Owner who lent the seat.

status.description: The account's status.

status_reason.description: Why it needs a reconnect, when known.

connection_location.description: Where it connects from: country, current_country, mode, strict.

quota.description: Present on RATE_LIMIT_ACCOUNT: the per-account request ceiling that was breached, with its name, the units remaining and total, and the absolute reset_time. Wait until reset_time before retrying.

toolset.description: Present on TOOLSET_DISABLED: the name of the toolset that is switched off for this tenant, so you can enable it or use another tool. Present on TOOL_REMOVED: the toolset of the tool that replaces the removed one (enable it if it is off), or null when the tool left MCP for the CLI and REST API only.

replacement.description: Present on TOOL_REMOVED (MCP only): the tool that replaces the removed one, to call instead with the arguments next_action describes, or null when it left MCP for the CLI and REST API only.

candidates.description: Present on AMBIGUOUS_IDENTIFIER: the entries the identifier matched. Pick one and re-send its id.

id.description: The id to send instead of the ambiguous identifier.

teams.description: Present on TEAM_REQUIRED (MCP only): the Teams you belong to. Re-send the call with the team argument set to one of their ids.

id.description: The Team id to pass as the team argument.

next_action.description: Present on errors that can be recovered programmatically, a plain sentence describing the next call to make.

notices.description: Present when something about this response is true but not visible in it. On a search, an entry names a filter value we could not check before sending it, or reports that some of the people on the page were not disclosed to the connected account, so an unexpected result count is explicable rather than silent. Branch on each entry's code, never on its message.

code.description: FILTER_VALUE_UNRESOLVED: the value matched no known filter option, so it was sent on as an id we could not check. FILTER_VALUE_UNCHECKED: the value already looked like an id, so it was never looked up, and this page came back empty. SOME_RESULTS_HIDDEN: some people on this page were not disclosed to the connected account, so those entries cannot be read back. ALL_RESULTS_HIDDEN: none of the people on this page were disclosed, so the page yielded nothing you can act on, even when more pages follow. PAGE_TRUNCATED: this page is short because the search stopped fetching upstream pages, not because the results ran out; follow cursor, and treat only a null cursor as the end.

message.description: One sentence explaining the condition and how to resolve it.

field.description: The request field the notice is about, dotted for nested filters.

example.message: The referenced resource does not exist for this tenant.

Message.description: A message. `quoted` carries the message this one quotes, when it quotes one; a quoted message has the same shape and may itself carry a `quoted`.

account_id.description: Account id that owns this message.

text.description: Full message text. Curviate does not keep it on the way out; reading a conversation back stores its message bodies in your tenant's inbox records, with no expiry.

attachments.description: Attachment descriptors (no bytes, use the attachment endpoint to download).

type.description: Attachment kind: file | img | video | audio.

unavailable.description: True when the attachment is no longer available.

is_sender.description: True if the connected account sent this message. Omitted when Curviate cannot yet identify the connected account; treat a missing value as unknown, not as received.

is_deleted.description: True if the message was deleted.

origin.description: Who sent a message the connected account sent: a Motion, the Unibox, the API (any API key or MCP grant), or LinkedIn itself. Derived by Curviate, never set by a caller. Omitted when unknown, and on received messages.

is_mentionned.description: True if the account is mentioned in this message.

reactions.description: Per-type reaction breakdown on the message.

reaction_count.description: Total reaction count across all types (derived).

provider.description: The platform this message originates from.

specifics.description: Platform-specific detail on the message. Carries `subject` for an InMail, which is set on the thread's opening message; absent or empty for an ordinary message.

subject.description: The message's subject line, when the platform carries one on this message. Typically an InMail opener, but an ordinary message sent with a subject carries one too. Reading a conversation back stores the subject in your tenant's inbox records alongside the body, with no expiry.

sender.description: The sender's profile, when the platform returned one alongside the message. sender_id always carries the identifier; this object carries the rest of what is known about that person.

public_identifier.description: The vanity slug from the profile URL, for example jane-smith. Present only when the request asks for it with expand=public_identifier, and then always present, carrying the slug or null when the platform surfaces none for this person.

specifics.description: Platform-enriched detail about the sender (for example connection distance, premium or verified status), when the platform returns it.

SequenceDocument.title: Sequence document v1
SequenceDocument.description: A Motion's Sequence: a flat steps array run from the first step, ending explicitly in "end". Served documents use this key order: $schema, on_reply, steps; in a step id, the kind key, timeout, save, save_to_contact, variants, with, event, then, else, next, note; in with post, newer_than, reaction, subject, text, note, note_fallback, fallback, withdraw_after; in a variant id, subject, text. A text holds at most 50 variables. Variables: `{{first_name}}` (any standard Contact field), `{{my_first_name}}`, `{{my_last_name}}`, `{{my_full_name}}` (the sending Account), any other `{{<key>}}` is the custom field `contact.extra.<key>`; the long forms `{{contact.<field>}}`, `{{contact.extra.<key>}}` and `{{account.<name>}}` stay valid; `{{enrollment.<name>}}` is a value a save of this Sequence writes. Delays are about their duration: every wait and until timeout gets a small random spread that only ever adds time.

event.description: Custom event sent once each time this step runs (not when skipped or failed), for example invite_sent.

note.description: Annotation shown in the builder graph. Never sent.

In the latter case the linkedin_sections value is not at fault, and the same request may succeed on another profile. INVALID_REQUEST also covers `mode=cache_only` sent together with `max_age`: that mode never reaches LinkedIn at any age, so a freshness threshold cannot change its answer, and the pair is refused rather than one of the two being ignored. Drop `max_age`, or use `mode=refill` (stored at any age, fetch only when nothing is stored). 403.description: Forbidden. LINKEDIN_FEATURE_NOT_SUBSCRIBED: the connected LinkedIn account's own subscription level does not entitle it to view this person's profile. This is the same condition a people-search result reports in-band as visibility:"hidden" on GET/POST .../search/..., reading a hidden result back always ends here. It is not a bug or a misconfiguration; retrying will not help, and there is no request shape that makes this person readable from this account. In a team, a call on an account a teammate connected can also answer INSUFFICIENT_ROLE (your role may not do this), ACCOUNT_NOT_SHARED (the teammate turned team access off for the account) or ACCOUNT_OWNER_ONLY (only the person who connected the account may do this). None is fixed by retrying.

A 429 on a budgeted action can also be BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, which is Curviate's own account-safety ceiling rather than a request-rate limit: it never reached LinkedIn, spent nothing, and carries row, reset_at and hint.

items.description: One thing you should know about this response.

code.description: EXPANSION_LIMIT_REACHED: more people on this page needed a profile lookup than one request performs, so the ones past the budget carry public_identifier null without ever having been looked up. Their null therefore does not mean the person has no public profile. Ask for a smaller page to resolve everyone. EXPANSION_WITHHELD_ACTIVITY_WINDOW: the profile lookups this page needed were refused because the account is outside its activity window at this hour and enforces it, so those people carry public_identifier null and their null does not mean they have no public profile either. Ask again inside the window, or widen the window on this account's safety policy. EXPANSION_WITHHELD_CEILING: the profile lookups this page needed were refused because the account's profile_views budget is at its configured ceiling and it enforces that, so those people carry public_identifier null and their null does not mean they have no public profile either. Raise the profile_views ceiling on this account's safety policy, or ask for a smaller page.

200.description: The connected account's home feed as agent-actionable posts. `sort=recent` (default) resolves each post's activity id + created_at + text + author name + post URL + kind, with engagement null; `sort=relevant` resolves the full shape (text, engagement, author id-triple). An empty feed is a valid 200 (items:[], cursor:null). Page until cursor is null.

activity_urn_id.description: The post's numeric activity id (no urn prefix), the primary durable handle to react/comment/fetch-detail, and the feed dedup key (the feed reorders; there is no disjoint-page guarantee). Both sorts.

author.description: The post's author. On `sort=recent` only `name` resolves (`type` is `other`, the rest null).

type.description: Person -> individual; company/showcase/sponsored -> organization; unresolved (every recent author) -> other.

posted_ago.description: Relative time label as rendered ("6d", "1w") or "Promoted" for sponsored posts. Locale-dependent. null on recent.

member_id.description: Obfuscated member id (ACoAA...), set for person authors (relevant).

numeric_id.description: Numeric member id, the strongest durable cross-action join key. Person authors (relevant).

company_id.description: Numeric company/organization id, organization authors (relevant), instead of a member id.

profile_url.description: Canonical profile URL.

text.description: Full post body, verbatim, on both sorts. null when the post has no body. Pass-through, never stored.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC datetime the feed activity was created, derived from the activity id (the same source as get-post's `created_at`). Both sorts. For a reshare this is when the reshare was made. null when the id does not carry a time.

post_url.description: Canonical post URL (recent). null on relevant.

kind.description: Post type parsed from the URL slug: ugcPost | share | groupPost | activity | post (recent). Open enum. null on relevant.

is_promoted.description: true for sponsored/promoted posts (relevant). Defaults false.

is_reshare.description: true if this post reshares another (relevant). Defaults false.

reshared_from.description: When `is_reshare`, the original post's { name, text }; else null.

text.description: Original post body (pass-through; never stored).

engagement.description: Engagement counts. Every count is null on recent, which cannot read them; use sort=relevant for counts. A null count is unknown, never zero.

likes.description: Reaction count, or null when the sort cannot read it.

comments.description: Comment count, or null when the sort cannot read it.

shares.description: Reshare count, or null when the sort cannot read it.

items.description: The feed posts, in feed order (for recent, appearance order == recency). [] for an empty feed (a 200 success). A page may return slightly more than `limit` (whole pages up to the next boundary).

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; null when the walk is exhausted. Self-describing of the sort, pass it back verbatim as `cursor`. The relevant cursor expires (~1h). There is no total (an unbounded, reordering stream); page until cursor is null.

200.description:
The notification card was deleted. This cannot be undone.

**Safe to retry.** Deleting a card you already deleted succeeds with 200 again, it is not an error, and it does not delete anything else. A client that retries after a network timeout is never punished for it. (A `card_urn` that never existed on this account is a 404; that distinguishes a wrong handle from a repeat.)

**Timing.** The removal takes effect within a few seconds; a notifications list read immediately after this call may still include the card for a moment. If you need to confirm removal, re-read after a short delay rather than instantly; but the 200 is already your confirmation that the card was resolved and the removal accepted.

200.description:
The 'show less like this' action was applied, the card is removed, exactly as `delete_notification` removes it. This cannot be undone.

**This is the same operation as delete.** LinkedIn's own web client sends an identical request for both its 'Delete notification' and its 'Show less like this' menu item, on every card type that offers them; there is no separate, softer signal available to send. This endpoint exists so the calling intent reads clearly; it does not behave differently. If you want fewer cards like this one in future, change the account's notification preferences on LinkedIn instead.

413.description: Payload too large. Three triggers, smallest first: the platform's own ceiling on total request size, which rejects bodies from roughly 1 MB and is the one most callers hit; then the caps enforced here, 5 MiB per attachment and 9 MiB for the whole request body. Base64 inflates a file by about 33 percent, so a 5 MiB file costs about 6.7 MiB of the body budget. Send fewer or smaller attachments; retrying the same request unchanged will not help.

read_window.description: The daily window sync reads happen in, in the account's time zone, which follows where the account connects (the same zone fields as the account's activity_window). schema.description: A LinkedIn post (content pass-through, text and attachments are never stored).

id.description: The post's own identifier as returned on this surface, use this value as the post_id path param on sub-resource endpoints. Its exact value can differ between two responses about the same post, so compare `urn` rather than `id` when you need to tell whether two responses describe one post.

urn.description: Stable identifier for the post itself, in `urn:li:activity:ID` or `urn:li:ugcPost:ID` form. Unlike `id`, this value is the same however you reached the post, so compare it to decide whether two responses describe the same post; a comment's `parent_post.urn` joins to it directly. For a repost it names the post being reshared, so reshares of one post share a `urn` while each keeps its own `created_at`. It is also accepted as the post_id path param on every operation that takes one, reads and writes alike, exactly like `id` is. null when the post carries no resolvable identity, and two nulls are not a match: treat null as unknown, never as equal.

title.description: Post title, or null if not set.

text.description: Full post text (content pass-through, never stored).

created_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC datetime this post was published, or null when it cannot be told reliably. Derived from the post's own activity identity, so it does not change with the route you used to reach it. null when the post carries no activity identity of its own (often a video or image post), never a guess. For a repost this is when the repost was made, not when the post it reshares was.

comment_count.description: Total comment count, or null when the platform hides it.

items.description: A per-reaction-type count bucket.

count.description: Count of this reaction type on the post.

reaction_count.description: Total reaction count, the sum of reactions[].count, or null when the platform hides it.

repost_count.description: Total repost count, or null when the platform hides it.

impressions_count.description: Total impression count, or null if not available.

user_reacted.description: The authenticated account's own reaction (unified lowercase enum), or null if not reacted.

author.description: Author of the post or comment. Two shapes reach this field, so read the display name as `name` when it is present and `display_name` otherwise.

name.description: Author's display name. Absent on the shape that carries `display_name` instead.

display_name.description: Author's display name. Absent on the shape that carries `name` instead.

object.description: Author entity discriminator, on the shape that carries one.

type.description: Author entity type (for example individual or organization), on the shape that carries one.

profile_picture_url.description: Author's profile picture URL, or null if not set.

written_by.description: The member who wrote the post (may differ from author for organization posts), or null.

permissions.description: Interaction permissions for the authenticated account, or null.

can_react.description: true if the account can react to this post.

can_share.description: true if the account can share this post.

can_post_comments.description: true if the account can comment on this post.

is_repost.description: true if this post is a repost of another post.

repost_id.description: id of the original post if is_repost is true, else null.

reposted_by.description: Profile of the account that reposted, or null.

repost_content.description: Embedded original post content for reposts, or null.

attachments.description: Media attachments on the post.

poll.description: Poll data if the post contains a poll, or null.

specifics.description: Job-posting or article context on the post, present only when applicable.

observed_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp for when this data was observed on LinkedIn. On a live fetch this is the time of the fetch; on a stored answer it is when the data was actually seen, not when you asked for it.

source.description: Whether this answer came from Curviate's stored copy or from a fresh LinkedIn fetch. A stored answer costs the connected account nothing and is never surfaced to the person being read. It also carries less: fields Curviate does not retain (message bodies, notes, attachments, third-party contact details) are only ever present on a live fetch. Pass mode=live when you need them.

withdrawn.description: Whether LinkedIn has told us this resource no longer exists, such as a removed profile. When true, the answer above is the copy Curviate still holds and must not be treated as current. Always present; false is the normal case.

withdrawn_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp for when a fetch MOST RECENTLY found this resource gone on LinkedIn. Every later fetch that finds it gone again moves it. Present only when withdrawn is true.

Three triggers, smallest first: the platform's own ceiling on total request size, which rejects bodies from roughly 1 MB and is the one most callers hit; then the caps enforced here, 5 MiB per attachment and 9 MiB for the whole request body. Base64 inflates a file by about 33 percent, so a 5 MiB file costs about 6.7 MiB of the body budget. Send fewer or smaller attachments; retrying the same request unchanged will not help.

Three triggers, smallest first: the platform's own ceiling on total request size, which rejects bodies from roughly 1 MB and is the one most callers hit; then the caps enforced here, 5 MiB per attachment and 9 MiB for the whole request body. Base64 inflates a file by about 33 percent, so a 5 MiB file costs about 6.7 MiB of the body budget. Send fewer or smaller attachments; retrying the same request unchanged will not help.

The day component differs by field on the classic profile's response: a work-experience end date carries a 29 day offset that can push the value into the following month, while a certification's expiry date uses day 01. Confirm against an entry whose real dates you know before deriving a month from the day here.

location.description: Where the role was based, as written on the profile.

description.description: The member's own description of the role. Passes through verbatim, never stored.

employment_type.description: Employment arrangement, e.g. PERMANENT, PERMANENT_PART_TIME, CONTRACT, CONTRACT_PART_TIME, FREELANCE, SELF_EMPLOYED, INTERNSHIP, APPRENTICESHIP, TEMPORARY, VOLUNTEERING. Not present on every entry.

workplace_type.description: Working arrangement: ON_SITE, HYBRID, or REMOTE. Not present on every entry.

skills.description: Skills the member associated with this role.

education.description: Present when requested via with_sections. parameters.description: Informational: which Curviate client sent the call (`sdk/<version>`, `cli/<version>`). It only feeds the dashboard's Integrations status lines and changes nothing about the request. The SDK and CLI send it for you.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of accounts to return per page (1-250, default 50).

200.description: A page of connected accounts plus the next-page cursor (null when exhausted).

account_id.description: Curviate account id (acc_...).

connection_location.description: Where LinkedIn sees this account connecting from. country: the configured country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), the one the account is set to use. current_country: the country of the connection in use right now; it differs from country only after a fallback, which can happen only when strict is false. mode: auto (a managed connection in country) or custom (your own proxy). strict: true when the account never connects from another country, null when unknown. Each field is null until known; an account connected through ip or your own proxy may show null until the next background refresh. Change it with PATCH /v1/accounts/{account_id} (country), or by reconnecting with country.

current_country.description: Country of the connection in use right now.

mode.description: auto: Curviate proxy. custom: your own proxy.

strict.description: true: never connects from another country.

checked_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC time of the last check that found where your own proxy connects from. Curviate checks it when you add it (one request through it) and then daily. Only each check's time, outcome, detected country and time zone are stored, for 30 days; the proxy's host, port, username, password and IP address are never stored. Null until a check found a country, and for a Curviate proxy.

detected_country.description: The country that check found (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Null until then.

flags.description: Warnings about where the account connects from. country_mismatch: it connects from another country than the location on its LinkedIn profile (your own proxy: the last detected country; a Curviate proxy: its current country). zone_moved: your own proxy's checks of the last 7 days fall in two or more time zones, for example after you changed the proxy. A flag changes nothing by itself: the account keeps its status and acts only in hours all its possible time zones share. Fix it with PATCH /v1/accounts/{account_id} and country or proxy. Empty when nothing is wrong.

status.description: Stable status whitelist.

auth_method.description: How the account last connected or reconnected successfully.

requested_products.description: The connection scope this account was last connected with (e.g. ["classic","company","sales_navigator","recruiter"]). owner_user_id.description: The user who connected this account. Only this person can reconnect it or solve its checkpoints. Null when unknown.

team_access.description: Whether the team's Owners and Managers may operate this account. True unless the person who connected it turned team access off.

metadata.description: Your own flat string map for this account, as last set by PATCH. Null when none.

substrate_created_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC creation timestamp of the underlying LinkedIn account, distinct from connected_at. Null until the first background enrichment lands.

quotas.description: Three of the account's safety rows, the ones a list shows: `connection_requests_no_note` (invitations, per week), `messages_first_degree` (messages, per day) and `inmail` (per day), each with `remaining`. window.description: Calendar grain this row is counted in. UTC, not account-local. `null` on the gauge, which has no window at all.

window_start.description: ISO-8601 UTC start of the current window; `null` on the gauge.

resets_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant the current window rolls over and `used` returns to 0. `null` on the gauge: a backlog falls when invitations are accepted or withdrawn, not at a window edge, so naming an instant would promise something nothing keeps.

used.description: Where the account stands: actions counted in the current window for a debit row, the summed tally for `total_actions`, the observed backlog for the gauge. remaining.description: `effective_ceiling` minus `used`, never below 0: what this account can still do on this row in the current window. Null when the row has no ceiling (`total_actions`) or no level yet (`pending_invites` before it was read).

effective_interface_ceiling.description: `interface_ceiling` with the account's warm-up ramp applied, and null wherever `interface_ceiling` is null. band.description: Where `used` sits against this row's own bands. `green` routine, `amber` at or past the routine band, `hard` at or past the warn-louder band, `over` at or past the ceiling, where the action is refused: limits are always enforced. over_default.description: Whether something on this row is configured above Curviate's own default. The safety policy carries the detail: which field, the value, the default and how well calibrated that default is.

halt.description: An active pause on this row because the platform refused a recent request on it, or `null`. reason.description: What the platform did: `rate_limited`, `platform_fault`, or `resend_cooldown` (the same invitation was sent too recently).

retry_after_seconds.description: Whole seconds until the pause expires.

observed_at.description: When the gauge's level was read from the platform. `null` on every other row, whose numbers are read live from Curviate's own records. Read it before acting on the backlog: the level is refreshed in the background, so it can be up to an hour old.

source.description: How well calibrated this row is, in descending order of trust: `substrate` (the transport layer's own guidance), `linkedin_official` (platform-published; reliable for mechanics such as credit counts and reset dates, not for safe volume), `practitioner` (corroborated operator experience), `inferred` (Curviate's own reasoning; flagged, never hidden), `unseeded` (no figure at all for this row on this account's limit profile, reported so nothing is silently missing, never presented as a number).

status_reason.description: Why the account is disconnected or needs a reconnect, when known. trial_ended: the free trial ended without a plan; the account and its Motions are kept, and signing it back in after choosing a plan keeps its id. proxy: your own proxy stopped working; replace it with PATCH proxy, or reconnect. Null otherwise.

Only `enabled` is settable (PATCH with `warm_up: {enabled}`); the other keys are derived, and sent back on a write they are accepted and ignored. Every warm-up number is inferred; none is published by LinkedIn. Curviate infers no account age.

enabled.description: The account's warm-up switch, default true. Off skips the connect ramp and the quiet ramp; recovery after a LinkedIn restriction still applies. Set it with PATCH /v1/{account_id}/safety-policy and `warm_up: {enabled}`, or with `warm_up` at connect.

state.description: `none` is an account at full speed. `ramping` is an account climbing 0.15, 0.35, 0.60, 0.85 to 1.00 by week after its connect or after a quiet spell. `restriction_recovery` is an account under, or just out of, a LinkedIn restriction: it holds at 0 for seven days after the restriction lifts, resumes at 0.40, then steps up 0.15 every four days.

factor.description: The multiplier applied to every row's ceiling: the lowest of every applying trigger's. 1 is not ramping.

week.description: Which week of the ramp supplies `factor`, counted from the connect or the return from a quiet spell, whichever is later. Null when no ramp applies or restriction recovery is lower.

steps.description: How many weeks the ramp has (5 today: 0.15, 0.35, 0.60, 0.85, 1.00). Read with `week` (0-based): week 1 is the second of `steps`.

triggers.description: The triggers that apply now: `connect` in the first 28 days after connect, `dormant` after more than 30 days with no action (counted from the connect when the account never acted) until the ramp it started completes, `post_restriction` under or recovering from a LinkedIn restriction. With warm-up off only `post_restriction` can apply.

dormant.description: True when the account has had no action for over 30 days (counted from its connect when it never acted), whether warm-up is on or off. With warm-up on, its next action starts the ramp at 0.15.

inmail_balance.description: The InMail credits LinkedIn last reported for this account, and when (`as_of`). Refreshed by every live InMail check and at connect; reading the account never calls LinkedIn. Null until a balance was observed, which on Basic can be never.

as_of.description: ISO-8601 UTC time of that reading.

motions_count.description: How many Motions (not archived) send from this account.

motion_refs.description: The first 20 of those Motions by name: `id` and `name`. Read GET /v1/motions?account_id= for all of them.

photo_url.description: The account's profile photo, a copy we store and refresh daily, so the URL does not expire; null when none is known.

profile_url.description: The account's own LinkedIn profile URL.

public_identifier.description: The slug in that URL.

location.description: The location on the account's LinkedIn profile, as LinkedIn shows it.

cursor.description: Next-page cursor; null on the last page.

400.description: limit out of range (1-250) or malformed cursor. TEAM_REQUIRED: an All-Teams key sent no X-Curviate-Team header (on an account route: with an account id that is not one); GET /v1/teams lists your teams.

Name the Team with the X-Curviate-Team header. GET /v1/teams lists yours.
Missing or invalid API key.

429.description: Rate limited, slow down and retry after the hinted delay.

value.message: The per-account request rate limit was exceeded; retry after the delay in retry_hint. A 429 on a budgeted action can also be BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, which is Curviate's own account-safety ceiling rather than a request-rate limit: it never reached LinkedIn, spent nothing, and carries row, reset_at and hint.
An unexpected internal error occurred.

get.description: List the team's LinkedIn accounts, cursor-paginated: `limit` 1-250 (default 50), `cursor` from the prior page (null on the last). Filter by `external_id`. One disconnected when its free trial ended stays listed (status_reason trial_ended); one you disconnected does not.

parameters.description: The account ID (`acc_...`) of the account to retrieve.

parameters.name: X-Curviate-Team
parameters.description: The team id to act in (GET /v1/teams lists yours). Required with an All-Teams key, except on account routes. A team key accepts only its own team.

profile_url.description: The account's own LinkedIn profile URL.

public_identifier.description: The slug in that URL.

location.description: The location on the account's LinkedIn profile, as LinkedIn shows it.

account_states.description: Platform conditions this LinkedIn account is currently in, additive to `status` and independent of it. `recruiter_session_evicted`: the account is signed in somewhere else and LinkedIn allows one session at a time for it, so a person has to close the other session; reconnecting will not help. `commercial_use_limited`: LinkedIn's commercial-use limit has tripped, so people search returns only a handful of results per query. It is a paywall, not a penalty, and nothing else about the account is affected. `profile_view_limited`: profile views outside this account's own network are being blocked; first-degree views still work. The two limits are detected from their symptom: LinkedIn publishes no threshold for either, exposes no counter, and lifts neither on request, so no number is reported. `commercial_use_limited` is a present-tense reading and a genuinely narrow search can also produce the shape it looks for, so treat it as a reason to check rather than a certainty; the next people search that returns a full page clears it. An account in none of these reports an empty array.

activity_window.description: The time zone the account's activity window is read in, derived from where it connects; outside the window Curviate refuses live writes to LinkedIn. Reads and anything served from Curviate's own store are never affected, at any hour. Set the hours on the account's safety policy.

effective_timezone.description: The IANA zone the activity window is read in, from where the account connects (its Curviate proxy's country, or your own proxy's detected location). Nobody sets it. Null while the zone is unknown: see fallback_timezones.

source.description: Where the zone came from: country (the connection country), region (a chosen region inside it), detected (a check of the proxy's location), or none (nothing yet).

zone_state.description: known: one zone. pinned: one zone a check agreed on, kept until the next location change. unknown: the account acts only in hours every zone in fallback_timezones shares; with none, it does not act until Curviate can tell where it connects from.

fallback_timezones.description: The candidate zones while zone_state is unknown, empty otherwise. Empty while unknown means the window is closed.

event_log.description: Where this account stands against the retained event log's row budget. Events are retained for 24 hours so you can read what the platform sent without running a listener; an account may hold at most row_cap of them at once. While at_row_cap is true, further events for this account are still delivered to any webhook you registered but are NOT retained, so the events resource stops being a complete record of what arrived. The budget is a backstop against a misbehaving upstream, sized so ordinary use never approaches it.

retained.description: Events currently held for this account. A level, not a total: retention is 24 hours, so this falls on its own as events age out.

row_cap.description: The maximum this account may hold at once.

at_row_cap.description: True while the cap is biting and incoming events are not being retained. Delivery to a registered webhook is unaffected.

save_connections_as_contacts.description: Whether Curviate saves this account's Connections as Contacts: each person becomes one Contact in your team, an existing Contact is only filled in, do-not-contact people are skipped. On by default. Absent when the account's plan has no Automate: nothing is saved then. Change it with PATCH.

save_connections_paused_reason.description: Why saving is stopped while save_connections_as_contacts is true: contact_limit_reached, your team holds its 100,000 Contacts. Delete Contacts you no longer need and saving resumes with the next synced Connections. null while saving. Absent with save_connections_as_contacts.

metrics.description: The latest daily snapshot of the account's own numbers, read once a day inside its activity window and stored, never read live on this request. null before the first snapshot. The history is GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}/metrics.

as_of.description: ISO-8601 UTC time the snapshot was read.

profile_viewers_90d.description: Profile viewers in the last 90 days.

search_appearances_week.description: Search appearances in the last completed week.

post_impressions_7d.description: Post impressions in the last 7 days.

ssi.description: The Social Selling Index, read for Sales Navigator accounts only; null for any other account or when it could not be read.

industry_rank_pct.description: Rank in the industry, as a top percentage.

network_rank_pct.description: Rank in the network, as a top percentage.

change_30d.description: Each of the four attention numbers minus its value in the latest snapshot at least 30 days older. null when there is no such snapshot yet; a field is null when either value is unknown.

account.summary: An active account with its budget view

degraded.summary: A connected account whose search has been capped by LinkedIn

patch.summary: Update an account's metadata or connection location

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: The account ID (`acc_...`) of the account to update.

parameters.name: X-Curviate-Team
parameters.description: The team id to act in (GET /v1/teams lists yours). Required with an All-Teams key, except on account routes. A team key accepts only its own team.

parameters.name: Curviate-Client
parameters.description: Informational: which Curviate client sent the call (`sdk/<version>`, `cli/<version>`). It only feeds the dashboard's Integrations status lines and changes nothing about the request. The SDK and CLI send it for you.

200.description: The updated account: the object GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} returns, without quotas and event_log (read those on GET). After a location change, connection_location is re-read from LinkedIn's side, so it shows where the account really connects from now. metadata, external_id and save_connections_as_contacts are stored by Curviate; a PATCH carrying only those makes no LinkedIn call.

auth_method.description: How the account last connected or reconnected successfully.

last_checked_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC time the account state was last checked.

seat_id.description: The seat this account occupies (null for an admin seatless account).

requested_products.description: The connection scope this account was last connected with (e.g. ["classic","company","sales_navigator","recruiter"]). A connect asks for every product and LinkedIn activates the ones the account actually has, so this is what was ASKED for, narrowed only by an explicit linkedin_premium on that connect. A linkedin_premium narrowing is not remembered between connects, so this shows what the LAST connect asked for and a reconnect that omits the field widens it again. Null for accounts connected before this was recorded; not attachment truth for Company Pages.

external_id.description: Your own id for this account's end user, as set on connect or PATCH. Null when none. Not unique.

owner_user_id.description: The user who connected this account. Only this person can reconnect it or solve its checkpoints. Null when unknown.

team_access.description: Whether the team's Owners and Managers may operate this account. True unless the person who connected it turned team access off.

metadata.description: Your own flat string map for this account, as last set by PATCH. Null when none.

connection_location.description: Where LinkedIn sees this account connecting from. country: the configured country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), the one the account is set to use. current_country: the country of the connection in use right now; it differs from country only after a fallback, which can happen only when strict is false. mode: auto (a managed connection in country) or custom (your own proxy). strict: true when the account never connects from another country, null when unknown. Each field is null until known; an account connected through ip or your own proxy may show null until the next background refresh. Change it with PATCH /v1/accounts/{account_id} (country), or by reconnecting with country.

current_country.description: Country of the connection in use right now.

mode.description: auto: Curviate proxy. custom: your own proxy.

strict.description: true: never connects from another country.

checked_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC time of the last check that found where your own proxy connects from. Curviate checks it when you add it (one request through it) and then daily. Only each check's time, outcome, detected country and time zone are stored, for 30 days; the proxy's host, port, username, password and IP address are never stored. Null until a check found a country, and for a Curviate proxy.

detected_country.description: The country that check found (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Null until then.

flags.description: Warnings about where the account connects from. country_mismatch: it connects from another country than the location on its LinkedIn profile (your own proxy: the last detected country; a Curviate proxy: its current country). zone_moved: your own proxy's checks of the last 7 days fall in two or more time zones, for example after you changed the proxy. A flag changes nothing by itself: the account keeps its status and acts only in hours all its possible time zones share. Fix it with PATCH /v1/accounts/{account_id} and country or proxy. Empty when nothing is wrong.

substrate_created_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC creation timestamp of the underlying LinkedIn account, distinct from connected_at. Null until the first background enrichment lands.

status_reason.description: Why the account is disconnected or needs a reconnect, when known. trial_ended: the free trial ended without a plan; the account and its Motions are kept, and signing it back in after choosing a plan keeps its id. proxy: your own proxy stopped working; replace it with PATCH proxy, or reconnect. Null otherwise.

warm_up.description: The account's ACTIVE warm-up, derived on every read. While warm-up holds an account back, every row's effective ceiling is its configured ceiling multiplied by `factor`, so a `factor` of 0.15 means the account is held to 15 percent of the numbers the rows report. Only `enabled` is settable (PATCH with `warm_up: {enabled}`); the other keys are derived, and sent back on a write they are accepted and ignored. This is separate from the per-row `warm_up_state` and `warm_up_factor`, which report what is active on that row: set `warm_up_factor` on a row to override the ramps (recovery after a restriction still caps it). Every warm-up number is inferred; none is published by LinkedIn. Curviate infers no account age.

enabled.description: The account's warm-up switch, default true. Off skips the connect ramp and the quiet ramp; recovery after a LinkedIn restriction still applies. Set it with PATCH /v1/{account_id}/safety-policy and `warm_up: {enabled}`, or with `warm_up` at connect.

state.description: `none` is an account at full speed. `ramping` is an account climbing 0.15, 0.35, 0.60, 0.85 to 1.00 by week after its connect or after a quiet spell. `restriction_recovery` is an account under, or just out of, a LinkedIn restriction: it holds at 0 for seven days after the restriction lifts, resumes at 0.40, then steps up 0.15 every four days.

factor.description: The multiplier applied to every row's ceiling: the lowest of every applying trigger's. 1 is not ramping.

week.description: Which week of the ramp supplies `factor`, counted from the connect or the return from a quiet spell, whichever is later. Null when no ramp applies or restriction recovery is lower.

steps.description: How many weeks the ramp has (5 today: 0.15, 0.35, 0.60, 0.85, 1.00). Read with `week` (0-based): week 1 is the second of `steps`.

triggers.description: The triggers that apply now: `connect` in the first 28 days after connect, `dormant` after more than 30 days with no action (counted from the connect when the account never acted) until the ramp it started completes, `post_restriction` under or recovering from a LinkedIn restriction. With warm-up off only `post_restriction` can apply.

dormant.description: True when the account has had no action for over 30 days (counted from its connect when it never acted), whether warm-up is on or off. With warm-up on, its next action starts the ramp at 0.15.

inmail_balance.description: The InMail credits LinkedIn last reported for this account, and when (`as_of`). Refreshed by every live InMail check and at connect; reading the account never calls LinkedIn. Null until a balance was observed, which on Basic can be never.

as_of.description: ISO-8601 UTC time of that reading.

motions_count.description: How many Motions (not archived) send from this account.

motion_refs.description: The first 20 of those Motions by name: `id` and `name`. Read GET /v1/motions?account_id= for all of them.

photo_url.description: The account's profile photo, a copy we store and refresh daily, so the URL does not expire; null when none is known.

profile_url.description: The account's own LinkedIn profile URL.

public_identifier.description: The slug in that URL.

location.description: The location on the account's LinkedIn profile, as LinkedIn shows it.

account_states.description: Platform conditions this LinkedIn account is currently in, additive to `status` and independent of it. `recruiter_session_evicted`: the account is signed in somewhere else and LinkedIn allows one session at a time for it, so a person has to close the other session; reconnecting will not help. `commercial_use_limited`: LinkedIn's commercial-use limit has tripped, so people search returns only a handful of results per query. It is a paywall, not a penalty, and nothing else about the account is affected. `profile_view_limited`: profile views outside this account's own network are being blocked; first-degree views still work. The two limits are detected from their symptom: LinkedIn publishes no threshold for either, exposes no counter, and lifts neither on request, so no number is reported. `commercial_use_limited` is a present-tense reading and a genuinely narrow search can also produce the shape it looks for, so treat it as a reason to check rather than a certainty; the next people search that returns a full page clears it. An account in none of these reports an empty array.

activity_window.description: The time zone the account's activity window is read in, derived from where it connects; outside the window Curviate refuses live writes to LinkedIn. Reads and anything served from Curviate's own store are never affected, at any hour. Set the hours on the account's safety policy.

effective_timezone.description: The IANA zone the activity window is read in, from where the account connects (its Curviate proxy's country, or your own proxy's detected location). Nobody sets it. Null while the zone is unknown: see fallback_timezones.

source.description: Where the zone came from: country (the connection country), region (a chosen region inside it), detected (a check of the proxy's location), or none (nothing yet).

zone_state.description: known: one zone. pinned: one zone a check agreed on, kept until the next location change. unknown: the account acts only in hours every zone in fallback_timezones shares; with none, it does not act until Curviate can tell where it connects from.

fallback_timezones.description: The candidate zones while zone_state is unknown, empty otherwise. Empty while unknown means the window is closed.

save_connections_as_contacts.description: Whether Curviate saves this account's Connections as Contacts: each person becomes one Contact in your team, an existing Contact is only filled in, do-not-contact people are skipped. On by default. Absent when the account's plan has no Automate: nothing is saved then. Change it with PATCH.

save_connections_paused_reason.description: Why saving is stopped while save_connections_as_contacts is true: contact_limit_reached, your team holds its 100,000 Contacts. Delete Contacts you no longer need and saving resumes with the next synced Connections. null while saving. Absent with save_connections_as_contacts.

moved.summary: Location moved to the United States

400.description: INVALID_REQUEST: a malformed proxy object; proxy together with country or allow_country_fallback; country on an account that uses your own proxy without proxy: null; allow_country_fallback alone on such an account; an unsupported country; ip (not changeable after connect; reconnect with ip instead); metadata over its limits (16 keys, key 40 chars, value 500); external_id outside 1-255 chars. CONNECTION_LOCATION_REQUIRED: proxy: null without country (clearing your own proxy alone would let the connection land anywhere). A proxy your request sent that refused its credentials, could not be reached or did not answer: the message names proxy and nothing changed. TEAM_REQUIRED: an All-Teams key sent no X-Curviate-Team header (on an account route: with an account id that is not one); GET /v1/teams lists your teams.

landedElsewhere.summary: Requested US, still connecting from Germany

value.message: This operation is not yet supported.

A refused location write carries details.account (status, status_reason, connection_location) as re-read.

patch.description: Updates metadata, external_id, whether its Connections are saved as Contacts, the connection location (country) or your own proxy (null plus a country returns to the Curviate proxy). Returns the account; connection_location is re-read after a location change.

metadata.description: Your own flat string map for this account (up to 16 keys, key 40 chars, value 500). Replaces the stored map whole; null clears it.

external_id.description: Your own id for this account's end user (1-255 chars), or null to clear it. Omit to leave it unchanged.

protocol.description: Proxy protocol. One of http, https, socks5, socks4.

password.description: Proxy auth password (optional). Passed to the connection only: never stored, logged or returned.

proxy.description: Your own proxy, or null to stop using it and return to the Curviate proxy (null requires country in the same request). Omit to leave it unchanged.

country.description: Move this account's connection location to this supported ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country (e.g. US, DE). LinkedIn sees a new IP in that country and may ask the owner to verify, so change it only when the current location is wrong. Strict unless allow_country_fallback is true. On an account using your own proxy, send proxy: null with it.

allow_country_fallback.description: Optional. false (the default with country or ip): only ever connect from that country; a connect fails when no connection is free there. true: a connection from another country may be used when none is free in the chosen one. Not accepted with proxy.

save_connections_as_contacts.description: Save this account's Connections as Contacts (Automate; on by default): each person becomes one Contact in your team, an existing Contact is only filled in, do-not-contact people are skipped. true also saves the Connections already synced; false keeps the Contacts saved so far.

200.description: One account's overview: who it is (profile), its own numbers (metrics, the daily snapshot), its limits and latest activity, and its results in the window as the team overview reads them scoped to it (performance, daily, its Motions). Each Contact counts once per Account and source. profile, metrics, limits and activity do not follow the window. No LinkedIn call. Default (no include, no fields), trimmed: profile (name, status, status_reason, warm_up.state, limit_profile), metrics (the four attention numbers, change_30d, as_of), performance (its rates and sends), limits (each row's used, effective_ceiling, remaining), the top 5 Motions by sent with each rate's numerator, denominator and rate, flags without values. include, fields, sort, limit and compare as on the team overview; account_attention and limit_reached flag this account.

account_id.description: The account filter when exactly one account is named; null otherwise (read account_ids).

account_ids.description: The account_id filter; [] when every visible account counts.

motion_ids.description: The motion_id filter of the overview; [] when every Motion counts.

origin.description: The origins counted (direct is unibox and api); null for every origin.

timezone.description: IANA zone the days are read in.

bucket.description: How daily is grouped (auto resolved: day up to 90 days, week up to 366, month beyond).

counts_only_through.description: YYYY-MM-DD, set when the window reaches back more than 12 months: up to and including this day the figures come from daily counts (UTC days); step and variant rates, seen and paths do not cover those days. null when every day is read in full detail.

paths_through.description: YYYY-MM-DD, the same day as counts_only_through: paths covers the days after it only, so past it paths does not add up to totals. null when paths covers the whole window.

generated_at.description: UTC instant of the read; outcomes so far and maturing are measured at it.

profile.description: Who the account is, now (not the window).

photo_url.description: The account's profile photo, a copy we store and refresh daily, so the URL does not expire; null when none is known.

profile_url.description: The account's own LinkedIn profile URL.

location.description: The location on the account's LinkedIn profile, as LinkedIn shows it.

status_reason.description: Why the account is disconnected or needs a reconnect, when known. trial_ended: the free trial ended without a plan; the account and its Motions are kept, and signing it back in after choosing a plan keeps its id. proxy: your own proxy stopped working; replace it with PATCH proxy, or reconnect. Null otherwise.

limit_profile.description: The LinkedIn plan the account's limits follow.

warm_up.description: The account's ACTIVE warm-up, derived on every read. While warm-up holds an account back, every row's effective ceiling is its configured ceiling multiplied by `factor`, so a `factor` of 0.15 means the account is held to 15 percent of the numbers the rows report. Only `enabled` is settable (PATCH with `warm_up: {enabled}`); the other keys are derived, and sent back on a write they are accepted and ignored. This is separate from the per-row `warm_up_state` and `warm_up_factor`, which report what is active on that row: set `warm_up_factor` on a row to override the ramps (recovery after a restriction still caps it). Every warm-up number is inferred; none is published by LinkedIn. Curviate infers no account age.

state.description: `none` is an account at full speed. `ramping` is an account climbing 0.15, 0.35, 0.60, 0.85 to 1.00 by week after its connect or after a quiet spell. `restriction_recovery` is an account under, or just out of, a LinkedIn restriction: it holds at 0 for seven days after the restriction lifts, resumes at 0.40, then steps up 0.15 every four days.

factor.description: The multiplier applied to every row's ceiling: the lowest of every applying trigger's. 1 is not ramping.

week.description: Which week of the ramp supplies `factor`, counted from the connect or the return from a quiet spell, whichever is later. Null when no ramp applies or restriction recovery is lower.

steps.description: How many weeks the ramp has (5 today: 0.15, 0.35, 0.60, 0.85, 1.00). Read with `week` (0-based): week 1 is the second of `steps`.

metrics.description: The latest daily snapshot of the account's own numbers, read once a day inside its activity window and stored, never read live on this request. null before the first snapshot. The history is GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}/metrics. null too when you may not operate the account.

as_of.description: ISO-8601 UTC time the snapshot was read.

profile_viewers_90d.description: Profile viewers in the last 90 days.

search_appearances_week.description: Search appearances in the last completed week.

post_impressions_7d.description: Post impressions in the last 7 days.

ssi.description: The Social Selling Index, read for Sales Navigator accounts only; null for any other account or when it could not be read.

industry_rank_pct.description: Rank in the industry, as a top percentage.

network_rank_pct.description: Rank in the network, as a top percentage.

change_30d.description: Each of the four attention numbers minus its value in the latest snapshot at least 30 days older. null when there is no such snapshot yet; a field is null when either value is unknown.

limits.description: The account's three outreach limits now (not the window): connection_requests_no_note (invitations, per week), messages_first_degree (messages, per day), inmail (InMails, per day), and its last InMail balance. null when you may not operate the account. Every row: GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}.

budget_row.description: The safety row. `search` counts result LINES, not queries issued; `content_poll` also debits `profile_views`. Two rows are not counters and say so in `kind`: `total_actions` is a tally of everything this account did in the window, and `pending_invites` is the outstanding invitation backlog read from the platform rather than something this account spends.

window.description: Calendar grain this row is counted in. UTC, not account-local. `null` on the gauge, which has no window at all.

used.description: Where the account stands: actions counted in the current window for a debit row, the summed tally for `total_actions`, the observed backlog for the gauge. A debit row with no activity reports 0, never null. Only the gauge can be `null`, and only before anything has observed it: 0 there would be a backlog nobody looked at.

effective_ceiling.description: What this row is ACTUALLY held to right now: `ceiling` with the account's warm-up ramp applied. Compare `used` against THIS one, and `band` is computed against it too. While warm-up holds an account back (its first four weeks after connect, after a quiet spell, or while it recovers from a restriction) the two differ, and in the first week after connect they differ by a factor of about seven. Equal to `ceiling` once the ramp is over, and `null` wherever `ceiling` is null. The account's ramp, its factor and the triggers behind it are on GET /v1/{account_id}/safety-policy as `warm_up`.

remaining.description: `effective_ceiling` minus `used`, never below 0: what this account can still do on this row in the current window. Null when the row has no ceiling (`total_actions`) or no level yet (`pending_invites` before it was read).

resets_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant the current window rolls over and `used` returns to 0. `null` on the gauge: a backlog falls when invitations are accepted or withdrawn, not at a window edge, so naming an instant would promise something nothing keeps.

band.description: Where `used` sits against this row's own bands. `green` routine, `amber` at or past the routine band, `hard` at or past the warn-louder band, `over` at or past the ceiling, where the action is refused: limits are always enforced. A row with no figures reports `green` at every value, because there is nothing to be past.

inmail_balance.description: The InMail credits LinkedIn last reported for this account, and when (`as_of`). Refreshed by every live InMail check and at connect; reading the account never calls LinkedIn. Null until a balance was observed, which on Basic can be never.

as_of.description: ISO-8601 UTC time of that reading.

activity.description: The account's latest 10 actions and their outcomes, newest first, whatever the window, within the last 12 months (the raw reach): invitations, messages and InMails sent, invitations accepted, replies. Source: origin, and the Motion for origin motion. Metadata only, never message text. The full feed: GET /v1/analytics/events?account_id=.

400.description: INVALID_REQUEST: an unknown query parameter, a malformed date (message starts from: or to:), from after to or a custom window over 3650 days (from:), range together with from or to (range:), an unknown range, bucket or origin, origin linkedin (never counted), or an unknown zone (timezone:). The grammar: a section this read does not have (include:), a path that is not a field or lies outside the returned sections (fields:), an unknown sort key (sort:), a limit outside 1 to 100 (limit:), a compare other than previous_period (compare:). TEAM_REQUIRED: an All-Teams key sent no X-Curviate-Team header (on an account route: with an account id that is not one); GET /v1/teams lists your teams.

value.message: A parameter failed validation.
Name the Team with the X-Curviate-Team header. GET /v1/teams lists yours.
Missing or invalid API key.

value.message: The targeted account is not on an active seat.

404.description: ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND: not one of your accounts, or removed. RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND: a motion_id is not one of your Motions. An id whose connection was replaced or removed also stops resolving here, and it is already absent from the list, so re-read `GET /v1/accounts` for the current id.

value.message: The referenced resource does not exist for this tenant.

429.description: Rate limited, slow down and retry after the hinted delay.

value.message: The per-account request rate limit was exceeded; retry after the delay in retry_hint. Per-team breaches carry RATE_LIMIT_TENANT; ingress-wide breaches (pre-auth, no per-client key) and upstream saturation both carry PLATFORM_RATE_LIMIT. A 429 on a budgeted action can also be BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, which is Curviate's own account-safety ceiling rather than a request-rate limit: it never reached LinkedIn, spent nothing, and carries row, reset_at and hint.

get.description: One account at a glance, no LinkedIn call: profile, its daily numbers, limits, latest activity (its last 10 actions within the last 12 months), and its results in the window (rates, daily, its Motions) with flags. include, fields, sort, limit and compare trim it as on GET /v1/analytics/motions.

Each field is null until known; an account connected through ip or your own proxy may show null until the next background refresh. Change it with PATCH /v1/accounts/{account_id} (country), or by reconnecting with country.

post.description: Authenticates a LinkedIn account with credentials or a cookie, nested: auth_method credentials reads credentials: { email, password }; auth_method cookie reads cookie: { li_at }. Omit account_id for a new account; include it to reconnect. Returns the account or a 202 checkpoint.

seat_id.description: The empty seat this NEW account will occupy. Required on a new connect; omit it and the call returns 400 INVALID_REQUEST with 'seat_id is required'. Seat ids look like seat_01H..., and every seat you own is listed by GET /v1/accounts/seats (any item with occupied false is free to use) and with click-to-copy in the seat table on your dashboard. Ignored when account_id is present, because a reconnect keeps the account on its current seat.

auth_method.description: How to authenticate. 'credentials' reads the nested `credentials` object (email + password). 'cookie' reads the nested `cookie` object (li_at) and also requires a top-level `user_agent`. Neither set of fields is accepted at the top level.

password.description: LinkedIn account password. Encrypted at rest, never logged.

credentials.description: Email + password authentication, supplied as a NESTED object (email and password do not go at the top level). Required when auth_method=credentials.

li_at.description: LinkedIn session cookie (li_at). Used for this connect only; never stored or logged.

li_a.description: Optional premium-session cookie (li_a) for Sales Navigator / Recruiter sessions. Used for this connect only; never stored or logged.

cookie.description: Session-cookie authentication, supplied as a NESTED object (li_at does not go at the top level). Required when auth_method=cookie, which also requires a top-level user_agent.

account_id.description: Present = re-authenticate this existing account in place (reconnect); omit = connect a new account.

linkedin_premium.description: Optional. Which LinkedIn premium surface this connection should ask for: 'sales_navigator' or 'recruiter'. Omit it and the connection asks for every product, and LinkedIn activates whichever ones the account actually has. One LinkedIn account can hold only one of the two premium surfaces, and when both are asked for Sales Navigator takes precedence, so set this to 'recruiter' if the account holds both and you want the Recruiter surface. This applies per connection and is not remembered: state it on every connect and reconnect where Recruiter must win.

timezone.description: Ignored. The account's time zone follows its connection location.

external_id.description: Your own id for the end user who owns this account, 1-255 chars, not unique. Treat it as opaque; avoid emails.

products.description: Optional allow-list of premium products to ask for: sales_navigator, recruiter. Omit to ask for both; [] asks for none. Classic LinkedIn and company pages are always included.

country.description: Where LinkedIn sees this account connecting from: a supported ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. US, DE; case-insensitive). Pick the country the account owner normally signs in from. A new connect needs exactly one of country, ip or proxy. Strict by default: the connect fails rather than use another country, unless allow_country_fallback is true.

ip.description: A public IPv4 address; its country becomes the connection location (strict by default). An alternative to country: send exactly one of country, ip or proxy on a new connect.

allow_country_fallback.description: Optional. false (the default with country or ip): only ever connect from that country; a connect fails when no connection is free there. true: a connection from another country may be used when none is free in the chosen one. Not accepted with proxy.

protocol.description: Proxy protocol. One of http, https, socks5, socks4.

password.description: Proxy auth password (optional). Passed to the connection only: never stored, logged or returned.

proxy.description: Your own proxy for this account's traffic. The proxy decides where LinkedIn sees the account connecting from, so country, ip and allow_country_fallback are not accepted with it.

user_agent.description: Exact browser User-Agent to pin for this account. REQUIRED for a cookie connect: send the User-Agent of the browser the li_at cookie was copied from. Optional for a credentials connect, where it helps an account that hits disconnection issues.

chats.description: Maximum number of chats to sync.

messages.description: Maximum number of messages to sync per chat.

sync_limit.description: Optional caps on how much history is synced for this account.

user_languages.description: Optional, cookie connects only: the language preferences of the browser the cookies came from, most preferred first (BCP 47 tags such as en-US, at most 5, each at most 35 characters). A credentials connect ignores it.

recruiter_contract_id.description: Which Sales Navigator or Recruiter contract this account sends from, for a LinkedIn account that holds several. Selected once the account is active; the answer then carries contract_selected (false: the account is connected but the contract could not be selected).

warm_up.description: Optional, new connects only, default true. false connects this account with warm-up off: no connect ramp and no ramp after a quiet spell; recovery after a LinkedIn restriction still applies. Change it later with PATCH /v1/{account_id}/safety-policy and warm_up.enabled.
