200.description: The events Curviate received for this account in the last 24 hours, newest received first. Events are retained whether or not any webhook is subscribed to them, which is what makes this readable with no listener running. Retention is 24 hours from received_at, absolute: an event is deleted on that clock and nothing extends it, including a live claim. Disconnecting an account removes its events from this response immediately. Each item carries its queue state, so state=done answers what your agents have already handled and state=unread answers what is still waiting. This read never claims anything.

id.description: The retained event's id. Also the value encoded in the next page's cursor.

event.description: The canonical event name, the same name you subscribe a webhook to (for example message.received, account.connected).

occurred_at.description: When the platform says the event happened. Events can arrive out of order, so do not treat this ordering as causal, establish ordering from the payload if you need it.

received_at.description: When Curviate received the event. Retention is 24 hours from this instant, absolute.

payload.description: Exactly the payload a registered webhook would have been delivered for this event, content included. It always carries account_id, event and occurred_at; the remaining fields depend on the event. This is the delivered payload itself, not a summary of it, and not the per-delivery envelope (there is no delivery when nothing is subscribed).

state.description: Queue state. unread: nobody holds it. claimed: leased to a consumer until lease_until, and an expired lease reads as unread again. done: handled, and it will never be handed out again. There is no failed state. Filter on it with the state query parameter, which is how you ask what your agents have already handled.

claimed_by.description: The consumer name recorded by the last claim, or null. Free text, never verified, so treat it as a label rather than an identity.

lease_until.description: When the current lease expires, or null when the event is not leased. A lease never extends the 24 hour retention.

done_at.description: When the event was marked done, or null. Set once and never moved.

items.description: Retained events for this account, newest received first. [] when nothing arrived in the last 24 hours.

cursor.description: Cursor for the next page; null on the terminal page. Pass it back verbatim. Page until cursor is null.

200.description: The event's state after being marked done. Done is the only terminal state there is, and it is shared: once an event is done it leaves the unread set for every consumer under this tenant, not just for you. There is no failed state, because an event nothing can handle simply expires with the rest at 24 hours. Calling this twice is safe and keeps the first done_at.

state.description: unread: claimable now. claimed: leased to someone until lease_until. done: handled, and it will never be handed out again. There is no failed state.

claimed_by.description: The consumer name recorded by the last claim, or null. Free text, never verified, so treat it as a label rather than an identity.

lease_until.description: When the current lease expires, or null when the event is not leased.

done_at.description: When the event was marked done, or null. Set once and never moved.

headers.description: Custom headers added to each delivery POST. Names must be valid HTTP header names and values must be printable ASCII (no line breaks or control characters). Reserved names are rejected at registration; they include Content-Type, User-Agent, Host, any Curviate-* or Sec-* name, and the hop-by-hop headers. At most 10 headers, 1024 characters per value, 4096 bytes in total. Custom headers are not covered by the delivery signature, so treat them as a hint, not as proof of origin. Values are encrypted at rest and are never returned by a read. A read shows the header name plus a 8-character keyed fingerprint of the value, which carries no part of the value and no indication of its length. It is deterministic within your account, so a fingerprint confirms a rotation took effect and tells you whether two of your webhooks carry the same credential; fingerprints are not comparable across accounts. The header name is what identifies which credential is configured.

200.description: The complete canonical event catalogue, grouped by source.

source.description: Event source group (messaging, user, account_status, post, recruiter, sales_nav).
Event source group.

linkedin_only.description: Present and true when the event carries LinkedIn-specific content.

availability.description: Delivery timing. Omitted (equivalent to 'realtime') on every live-pushed event. 'no_longer_realtime' means no push exists for this event; 'not_realtime' means delivery is not guaranteed sub-second and may lag the underlying LinkedIn event, typically because it is detected by a poll rather than pushed, though a given event's own reference article may document an additional immediate path.

events.description: An inbound message arrived in any chat (classic / InMail).
A message in a chat was read by the recipient.
A reaction was added to a message.
A message was edited after send.
A message was deleted.
A chat's container state changed (e.g. archived, muted, read-state); useful for inbox automation.
A chat thread was deleted.

A pending invitation sent through Curviate (by a Motion or a direct send) was accepted by the recipient. Detected by Curviate's own polling, not real-time: latency up to about 160 in-window minutes while Motion invitations are pending, about 580 otherwise, longer while an account warms up.

A new relation appeared on the account (any new LinkedIn connection, not just ones you invited). Polled, not real-time; up to ~4h delay; a freshly connected account may see a backfill burst of these on first connect.
A new account link completed successfully for the first time.
The account is in a healthy, connected state. Also sent when a connect reactivates an account you had previously disconnected and it comes back healthy.
A synchronization cycle completed successfully. No longer pushed in real time, v2 has no equivalent event; no read-path alternative exists.
An existing account was re-authorized in place. Reactivating an account you had previously disconnected does not send this event; that connect reports the state the account comes back in.
Credentials expired, the account needs reconnection. Carries status_reason, null when the cause is unknown.

The account is connected, but some actions on it fail: LinkedIn restricted the account, or one LinkedIn product on it (such as Sales Navigator or Recruiter) needs re-authentication or is failing. Surface it to a human. If a single product is failing, a reconnect may restore it. A LinkedIn restriction is usually detected by a daily account reconciliation (within about 24 hours) or immediately by a connect; a failing product is reported immediately. An on-demand account read always reports the current state.
The initial account-link attempt failed terminally. No longer pushed in real time, detect via an on-demand account read.

The account is in the disconnected state and cannot act until it is reconnected. This includes an explicit disconnect or deletion, and a connect or reconnect attempt that observes an already-disconnected account without removing it. Where the account was actually removed, its id will 404 on a later read. Carries status_reason: trial_ended when the free trial ended without a plan (the account is kept and keeps its id when signed back in), else null.
Account synchronization encountered an error (not a credentials issue, needs investigation). Carries status_reason: proxy when your own proxy failed, else null.
Account synchronization was stopped or paused externally. No longer pushed in real time, v2 has no equivalent event; detect via an on-demand account read.
An account link is in progress. Transient and high-frequency, opt in explicitly. No longer pushed in real time, v2 has no equivalent event.
A LinkedIn-side scope the account relies on was withdrawn. No longer pushed in real time, detect via an on-demand account read.
The initial history backfill for a newly connected account has started (informational, bracket-open).
The initial history backfill completed, full LinkedIn history is now queryable.
The initial history backfill failed. The delivered payload carries a neutral `reason`, one of `internal`, `proxy`, or `provider`.
A scheduled post was published. Carries draft_id, post_id (null when none was returned), account_id, scheduled_at, and published_at. Never carries the post text or media.

A scheduled post could not be published. Carries draft_id, account_id, scheduled_at, failure_code, and failure_message. Never carries the post text or media. A failure_code of outcome_unknown means the publish call timed out or ended without a usable answer after the request was sent; the post may be live, so check the account's posts before retrying.
A Motion changed status. Carries motion_id, motion_name, from, to, reason, reason_message and changed_by_user_id, with account_id null.

A candidate was added to a hiring project pipeline.
A candidate pipeline status changed.
An InMail arrived on a Sales Navigator seat.

enabled.description: A disabled webhook is kept but delivers nothing. Disabling takes effect immediately, including for retries that were already queued; those attempts are abandoned, not deferred, so re-enabling delivers new events rather than replaying the ones that were dropped.

value_fingerprint.description: A 8-character keyed fingerprint of the configured value. It carries no part of the value and no indication of its length, but it is not a zero-disclosure field: it is deterministic, so two headers in your account with the same fingerprint hold the same value, and a changed fingerprint means a changed value. Use it to confirm a rotation took effect, or to tell whether two of your webhooks carry the same credential. Fingerprints are scoped to your account and are not comparable with another account's. Null for a header configured before fingerprints existed. The header name is what identifies which credential is configured.

headers.description: Custom headers added to each delivery POST. Values are encrypted at rest and no read returns one, so a read shows the name and a fingerprint of the value.

events.description: Canonical event names this webhook subscribes to.

data.description: Field-remapping keys for the delivery payload (messaging and user sources only; post and account_status have none).

secret_prefix.description: First 8 characters of the signing secret. The full secret is never returned on edit, it is preserved unchanged.

disabled_reason.description: failing: Curviate switched this webhook off after 3 days of failed deliveries (one email went to its creator). Switching it on clears it. null otherwise.

failing_since.description: When the first failed attempt after the last success happened (ISO 8601). A delivery that ends failed 72 hours or more after it switches the webhook off. null when not failing; any success clears it.

last_delivery_status_code.description: The HTTP status of the latest delivery attempt. null when none was made, or no response came back (a timeout, a network error, a refused address).

created_by.description: The Team member who created the webhook; null when none is recorded.

account_ids.description: Accounts targeted by this webhook (acc_ ids you own), or null when it covers every account its creator can operate, now and later (any source).

motion_ids.description: When set, only events whose data.motion_id is one of these Motions (mot_ ids) are delivered. null: no Motion filter.

body_template.description: The body template as written (a JSON text with {{variables}}); null: the standard payload. See https://docs.curviate.com/reference/webhooks/body-templates

custom_event_names.description: motion source: the motion.custom_event names delivered; null: every one.

enabled.description: A disabled webhook is kept but delivers nothing. Disabling takes effect immediately, including for retries that were already queued; those attempts are abandoned, not deferred, so re-enabling delivers new events rather than replaying the ones that were dropped.

value_fingerprint.description: A 8-character keyed fingerprint of the configured value. It carries no part of the value and no indication of its length, but it is not a zero-disclosure field: it is deterministic, so two headers in your account with the same fingerprint hold the same value, and a changed fingerprint means a changed value. Use it to confirm a rotation took effect, or to tell whether two of your webhooks carry the same credential. Fingerprints are scoped to your account and are not comparable with another account's. Null for a header configured before fingerprints existed. The header name is what identifies which credential is configured.

headers.description: Custom headers added to each delivery POST. Values are encrypted at rest and no read returns one, so a read shows the name and a fingerprint of the value.

events.description: Canonical event names this webhook subscribes to.

data.description: Field-remapping keys for the delivery payload (messaging and user sources only; post and account_status have none).

secret_prefix.description: First 8 characters of the signing secret. The full secret is never returned on edit, it is preserved unchanged.

disabled_reason.description: failing: Curviate switched this webhook off after 3 days of failed deliveries (one email went to its creator). Switching it on clears it. null otherwise.

failing_since.description: When the first failed attempt after the last success happened (ISO 8601). A delivery that ends failed 72 hours or more after it switches the webhook off. null when not failing; any success clears it.

last_delivery_status_code.description: The HTTP status of the latest delivery attempt. null when none was made, or no response came back (a timeout, a network error, a refused address).

warnings.description: On an edit that sets a body_template: its warnings (TW1), in the errors[] entry shape plus line and col; [] when none. Absent on a read.

400.description: Invalid request, malformed URL, empty events array, event-source mismatch, a change to the immutable source, or a malformed id. TEAM_REQUIRED: an All-Teams key sent no X-Curviate-Team header (on an account route: with an account id that is not one); GET /v1/teams lists your teams.

value.message: A parameter failed validation.
Name the Team with the X-Curviate-Team header. GET /v1/teams lists yours.
Missing or invalid API key.

402.description: Payment required, an active subscription is needed.

value.message: An active subscription or seat is required.

404.description: Webhook not found, or one or more account_ids not found for this tenant.

value.message: The referenced resource does not exist for this tenant.

413.description: Payload too large, the request body exceeds the size limit.

value.message: Request body is too large: it exceeds the 9437184-byte limit.

422.description: WEBHOOK_TEMPLATE_INVALID: the body_template fails the lint; nothing is saved. errors[] holds every finding at once, with line and col.

429.description: Rate limited, slow down and retry after the hinted delay.

value.message: The per-account request rate limit was exceeded; retry after the delay in retry_hint. Per-team breaches carry RATE_LIMIT_TENANT; ingress-wide breaches (pre-auth, no per-client key) and upstream saturation both carry PLATFORM_RATE_LIMIT. A 429 on a budgeted action can also be BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, which is Curviate's own account-safety ceiling rather than a request-rate limit: it never reached LinkedIn, spent nothing, and carries row, reset_at and hint.

patch.description: Update a webhook in place. Every field is optional, a provided field replaces its value, an omitted field is left unchanged. The source is immutable and the signing secret is preserved (never re-issued).

events.description: Replace the subscribed events (whole-array). Every event must be a canonical event whose source matches the webhook's source.

request_url.description: Replace the delivery URL. Must be a publicly reachable https host on the default https port. The URL is stored encrypted and read back masked (https://host/•••); PATCHing the masked value keeps the stored URL.

name.description: Replace the human-readable name (1-100 chars), or null to clear it.

enabled.description: Enable or disable the webhook. A disabled webhook delivers nothing. Disabling is a stop, not a pause: it takes effect immediately, including for retries that were already queued, and those attempts are abandoned rather than deferred, so re-enabling delivers new events instead of replaying the ones that were dropped.

headers.description: Replace the custom headers added to each delivery POST (whole-array). An entry with a key and no value keeps that header's stored value; a new key needs a value. Names must be valid HTTP header names and values must be printable ASCII (no line breaks or control characters). Reserved names are rejected at registration; they include Content-Type, User-Agent, Host, any Curviate-* or Sec-* name, and the hop-by-hop headers. At most 10 headers, 1024 characters per value, 4096 bytes in total. Custom headers are not covered by the delivery signature, so treat them as a hint, not as proof of origin. Values are encrypted at rest and are never returned by a read. A read shows the header name plus a 8-character keyed fingerprint of the value, which carries no part of the value and no indication of its length. It is deterministic within your account, so a fingerprint confirms a rotation took effect and tells you whether two of your webhooks carry the same credential; fingerprints are not comparable across accounts. The header name is what identifies which credential is configured.

data.description: Replace the field-remapping keys for the delivery payload (whole-array).

account_ids.description: Replace the targeted accounts (whole-array, each an acc_ id you own), or null to cover every account you can operate, now and later.

motion_ids.description: Only deliver events whose data.motion_id is one of these Motions (mot_ ids you own, up to 100). Events that carry no Motion are then not delivered. Replaces the whole list; null removes the filter.

body_template.description: The delivery body as a JSON text with {{variables}} inside its strings (GET /v1/webhooks/variables lists them per source); null (the default) sends the standard payload. Signed over the rendered bytes, sent as application/json, at most 16,384 bytes and 200 variables, read back as written. Excludes data remapping. A template that fails the lint answers 422 WEBHOOK_TEMPLATE_INVALID with every finding in errors[]. See https://docs.curviate.com/reference/webhooks/body-templates

custom_event_names.description: With motion.custom_event in events: null (the default) delivers every custom event, a list only those names (up to 50). GET /v1/webhooks/events lists the names your Sequences send under custom_events.

disable.summary: Disable a webhook (delivers nothing until re-enabled)

changeUrlAndEvents.summary: Replace the delivery URL and the subscribed events

coverAllAccounts.summary: Switch a webhook to every account you can operate, now and later

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: The account ID (`acc_...`) whose safety policy to read.

parameters.name: X-Curviate-Team
parameters.description: The team id to act in (GET /v1/teams lists yours). Required with an All-Teams key, except on account routes. A team key accepts only its own team.

parameters.name: Curviate-Client
parameters.description: Informational: which Curviate client sent the call (`sdk/<version>`, `cli/<version>`). It only feeds the dashboard's Integrations status lines and changes nothing about the request. The SDK and CLI send it for you.

200.description: The account's full safety policy: every configurable field for every budget row, in one response. Any row whose configured value is above the Curviate default carries an `over_default` entry naming the value, the default and the source class of that default. Two top-level fields are DERIVED rather than configured: `warm_up` says whether Curviate is currently holding this account below its configured ceilings and by how much, and `activity_window` says which time zone the window is read in, from where the account connects.

account_id.description: The account this policy governs.

limit_profile.description: Which set of Curviate defaults every row below is resolved from. Each profile inherits the one before it and raises a few rows: `premium` adds a daily invitation band and open-profile InMail, `sales_navigator` raises profile views and search, `recruiter` raises profile views again. This is the platform product active on the account, not the Curviate seat entitlement. The two can disagree, and this is the one that governs the numbers. The elevated Sales Navigator and Recruiter figures apply only to calls made through the matching interface, the `/v1/{account_id}/sales-navigator/...` and `/v1/{account_id}/recruiter/...` operations, and Curviate holds each call to the figure for the interface it goes through. The numbers here are therefore the ones a standard-interface call is held to, on every profile; a call through one of those operations resolves from the elevated set instead, and each row publishes that figure as `interface_ceiling`.

limit_profile_source.description: Where `limit_profile` came from. `detected`: Curviate read it from LinkedIn, at `limit_profile_detected_at`. `operator`: it was set through this operation and holds until you release it by sending `limit_profile_source: "default"` on this operation, on its own (changing `limit_profile` and releasing it in the same request is refused). Nothing else overrides it: a connect, a reconnect and an account read all leave a pinned value exactly as you set it. `default`: it has never been observed, so the value is the seeded `basic` and says nothing about the account; Curviate detects it on the account's next read or connect.

limit_profile_detected_at.description: When Curviate last read `limit_profile` from LinkedIn, whether or not the value changed. Null until it has. Curviate re-reads it on connect and, at most once a day, on an account read, so a subscription change reaches the numbers without a reconnect. While `limit_profile_source` is `operator` neither the value nor this timestamp moves, until you release the pin.

warm_up.description: The account's ACTIVE warm-up, derived on every read. While warm-up holds an account back, every row's effective ceiling is its configured ceiling multiplied by `factor`, so a `factor` of 0.15 means the account is held to 15 percent of the numbers the rows report. Only `enabled` is settable (PATCH with `warm_up: {enabled}`); the other keys are derived, and sent back on a write they are accepted and ignored. This is separate from the per-row `warm_up_state` and `warm_up_factor`, which report what is active on that row: set `warm_up_factor` on a row to override the ramps (recovery after a restriction still caps it). Every warm-up number is inferred; none is published by LinkedIn. Curviate infers no account age.

enabled.description: The account's warm-up switch, default true. Off skips the connect ramp and the quiet ramp; recovery after a LinkedIn restriction still applies. Set it with PATCH /v1/{account_id}/safety-policy and `warm_up: {enabled}`, or with `warm_up` at connect.

state.description: `none` is an account at full speed. `ramping` is an account climbing 0.15, 0.35, 0.60, 0.85 to 1.00 by week after its connect or after a quiet spell. `restriction_recovery` is an account under, or just out of, a LinkedIn restriction: it holds at 0 for seven days after the restriction lifts, resumes at 0.40, then steps up 0.15 every four days.

factor.description: The multiplier applied to every row's ceiling: the lowest of every applying trigger's. 1 is not ramping.

week.description: Which week of the ramp supplies `factor`, counted from the connect or the return from a quiet spell, whichever is later. Null when no ramp applies or restriction recovery is lower.

steps.description: How many weeks the ramp has (5 today: 0.15, 0.35, 0.60, 0.85, 1.00). Read with `week` (0-based): week 1 is the second of `steps`.

triggers.description: The triggers that apply now: `connect` in the first 28 days after connect, `dormant` after more than 30 days with no action (counted from the connect when the account never acted) until the ramp it started completes, `post_restriction` under or recovering from a LinkedIn restriction. With warm-up off only `post_restriction` can apply.

dormant.description: True when the account has had no action for over 30 days (counted from its connect when it never acted), whether warm-up is on or off. With warm-up on, its next action starts the ramp at 0.15.

activity_window.description: The zone the activity window is read in, derived from where the account connects. Outside the window, a live write to LinkedIn is refused; reads and anything served from Curviate's own store are never affected, at any hour. Read-only: a write accepts it back and ignores it, so a read policy can be sent back unchanged.

effective_timezone.description: The IANA zone the activity window is read in, from where the account connects (its Curviate proxy's country, or your own proxy's detected location). Nobody sets it. Null while the zone is unknown: see fallback_timezones.

source.description: Where the zone came from: country (the connection country), region (a chosen region inside it), detected (a check of the proxy's location), or none (nothing yet).

zone_state.description: known: one zone. pinned: one zone a check agreed on, kept until the next location change. unknown: the account acts only in hours every zone in fallback_timezones shares; with none, it does not act until Curviate can tell where it connects from.

fallback_timezones.description: The candidate zones while zone_state is unknown, empty otherwise. Empty while unknown means the window is closed.

active_hours.description: This account's active hours in force for an action type with no edges of its own: its own `active_hours` when set (source `account`), else the Team's (`team`), else Curviate's default, Monday to Friday 07:00 to 22:00 (`default`). Set it here; null falls back to the Team's. Live writes happen only on these days, between start and end, in each account's own time zone; each edge varies by up to 45 minutes a day. Write `{days, start, end}` (at least one day, start and end different, an end before the start wraps past midnight) or null to clear; no days, equal edges, an unknown day or a time that is not HH:MM is a 400. `source` is read-only: sending the read back changes nothing.

days.description: The active days, in week order.

source.description: Where these hours come from: `account`, `team` or `default`.

budget_row.description: The counted-action row this policy governs.

ceiling.description: What this row refuses at (limits are always enforced), in the row's own unit. Null means the row is uncalibrated: Curviate has no figure for it.

window_kind.description: The calendar grain this row is counted in.

window_span.description: How many grain units one counting window spans.

window_timezone.description: IANA zone name the counting window is aligned to. Null counts in UTC.

activity_window_start.description: Local HH:MM this row's activity window opens: the hours in force, from the rung `activity_window_source` names.

activity_window_end.description: Local HH:MM this row's activity window closes, from the same rung.

activity_window_source.description: Where this row's hours come from, the first rung that is set: `account_row` (this row's own edges on the account), `account` (the account's `active_hours`), `team_row` (the Team's row default), `team` (the Team's `active_hours`) or `default` (07:00 to 22:00). Read-only. A row's own edges never change the days: those are the `active_hours` below it.

activity_window_applies_to.description: What the activity window governs. `writes` (the default) covers live writes to LinkedIn; `all` widens it to live reads as well, which is the setting for a persona that should not be seen browsing at 03:00. It is broader than it sounds: `all` covers every live read, including the ones about the account itself, so a nightly analytics or invitation-backlog poll is refused at 03:00 too. A read Curviate answers from its own store never reaches LinkedIn, so it is never subject to the window under either setting, at any hour; the same read IS covered when the store cannot answer it, or when you ask for it live. Inbound events are never subject to it either. One action set to `all` reaches the whole account's live reads that spend no budget of their own (notifications, profile analytics, SSI, profile visitors, the invitation and saved-list listings): those calls debit no action type, so they have none to read this setting from and take the account-wide answer instead. Reads that DO debit an action type read that action type's own setting.

warm_up_state.description: The warm-up state ACTIVE on this row: the label for `warm_up_factor` beside it, so the two always agree. Read-only, so a value sent on a write is accepted and ignored; set `warm_up_factor` to pin this row's ramp.

warm_up_factor.description: The multiplier ACTIVE on this row, which is what `effective_ceiling` above was computed with. 1 is not ramping. Set it to pin this row and ignore the account's derived ramps; leave it unset to follow the derivation. Recovery after a LinkedIn restriction still caps it: while the account recovers, the lower of the two applies.

character_cap.description: Length cap on the row's free-text field, in characters.

subject_character_cap.description: Length cap on the row's subject line, in characters.

per_query_cap.description: Bound on a single query's result lines. Search rows only.

source_class.description: How well calibrated this row's number is. `unseeded` means Curviate has no green, amber or ceiling figure for this row on this profile: the row is reported so nothing is silently missing, but nothing has calibrated it, so no value you set can be `over_default`.

effective_ceiling.description: What this row is ACTUALLY held to right now: `ceiling` with the account's warm-up ramp applied. Read this one, not `ceiling`, to know where the next call will be stopped. On an account in warm-up the two differ, and in the first week after connect they differ by a factor of about seven. Null when the row has no ceiling to ramp. `warm_up_state` and `warm_up_factor` beside it are the values ACTIVE on this row, not the seeded ones.

interface_ceiling.description: What a call through the matching ELEVATED interface is held to on this row: the `/v1/{account_id}/sales-navigator/...` and `/v1/{account_id}/recruiter/...` operations. Null when this row and limit profile have no such figure, which is every row on `basic` and `premium` and most rows everywhere. Everything else on this row (`ceiling`, `effective_ceiling`, `band` and `over_default`) is the STANDARD-interface figure, because one counter serves both interfaces and the standard side is the conservative one to band against. The consequence is worth reading: on a `sales_navigator` or `recruiter` account a row can report `band: "over"` with `posture: "enforce"` while a call through the elevated interface still succeeds; the refusal the band predicts is the one a standard call gets.

effective_interface_ceiling.description: `interface_ceiling` with the account's warm-up ramp applied, and null wherever `interface_ceiling` is null. Read THIS to know where an elevated-interface call stops, for the same reason `effective_ceiling` rather than `ceiling` answers that for a standard one.

items.description: One configured value that exceeds Curviate's own seeded default. Present for as long as the value is above default; there is no acknowledgement that clears it. Setting the value back to the default removes it.

field.description: The field whose configured value is above default.

source_class.description: How well calibrated the DEFAULT is. `substrate` and `linkedin_official` are published figures; `practitioner` is corroborated operator experience; `inferred` is our own reasoning; `unseeded` means we have no figure at all for that row, in which case there is nothing to be above and no entry appears. Read this before deciding whether being above default matters.

over_default.description: Empty when nothing on this row is above default. Computed against the STANDARD-interface default, like `band` and for the same reason.

pacing.description: How Curviate paces Motion actions on this account: before a Motion action of a type, at least `min_gap_seconds` plus a random part of `jitter_seconds` must have passed since the account's previous Motion action of that type, and `global.min_gap_seconds` since its previous Motion action of any type or its previous LinkedIn write through the API. `read` covers profile and post reads. Direct API calls are never paced: those are yours to pace. Values resolve per field from Curviate's default, then the team's, then this account's. Write any subset as `pacing: {"invite.send": {"min_gap_seconds": 600}}`; null clears a field or a whole type back to the default. Values are whole seconds from 0 to 86400 and are never clamped; an unknown type or field, a fraction or an out-of-range value is a 400 naming it.

min_gap_seconds.description: The least time between two Motion calls of this type on the account, in seconds.

jitter_seconds.description: A random extra of up to this many seconds added to each gap. Absent on `global`, which has no jitter.

items.description: One pacing value set BELOW Curviate's default: a shorter gap paces the account more aggressively. The rows' own warning shape.

field.description: The pacing field set below default.

code.description: The key was removed: limits are always enforced. Stop sending it.

field.description: The removed key the request sent.

message.description: What was removed and the last day it is accepted.

seeded.summary: A freshly connected account, entirely on the seeded defaults

overDefault.summary: A ceiling configured far above the default, with the warning that follows it

400.description: TEAM_REQUIRED: an All-Teams key sent no X-Curviate-Team header (on an account route: with an account id that is not one); GET /v1/teams lists your teams.

value.message: Name the Team with the X-Curviate-Team header. GET /v1/teams lists yours.

404.description: No such account for this tenant. An id whose connection was replaced or removed also stops resolving here, and it is already absent from the list, so re-read `GET /v1/accounts` for the current id.

value.message: The referenced resource does not exist for this tenant.

429.description: Rate limited, slow down and retry after the hinted delay.

value.message: The per-account request rate limit was exceeded; retry after the delay in retry_hint. Per-team breaches carry RATE_LIMIT_TENANT; ingress-wide breaches (pre-auth, no per-client key) and upstream saturation both carry PLATFORM_RATE_LIMIT. A 429 on a budgeted action can also be BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, which is Curviate's own account-safety ceiling rather than a request-rate limit: it never reached LinkedIn, spent nothing, and carries row, reset_at and hint.

get.description: Returns every configurable safety field for every budget row of this account: ceiling, bands, window, warm-up, and where each value was inherited from. Limits are always enforced. Fields and precedence: /reference/safety.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: The account ID (`acc_...`) whose safety policy to update.

parameters.name: X-Curviate-Team
parameters.description: The team id to act in (GET /v1/teams lists yours). Required with an All-Teams key, except on account routes. A team key accepts only its own team.

parameters.name: Curviate-Client
parameters.description: Informational: which Curviate client sent the call (`sdk/<version>`, `cli/<version>`). It only feeds the dashboard's Integrations status lines and changes nothing about the request. The SDK and CLI send it for you.

200.description: The account's full safety policy: every configurable field for every budget row, in one response. Any row whose configured value is above the Curviate default carries an `over_default` entry naming the value, the default and the source class of that default. Two top-level fields are DERIVED rather than configured: `warm_up` says whether Curviate is currently holding this account below its configured ceilings and by how much, and `activity_window` says which time zone the window is read in, from where the account connects. This is the same body the read returns, so a value set above default is reported on the write that set it.

account_id.description: The account this policy governs.

limit_profile.description: Which set of Curviate defaults every row below is resolved from. Each profile inherits the one before it and raises a few rows: `premium` adds a daily invitation band and open-profile InMail, `sales_navigator` raises profile views and search, `recruiter` raises profile views again. This is the platform product active on the account, not the Curviate seat entitlement. The two can disagree, and this is the one that governs the numbers. The elevated Sales Navigator and Recruiter figures apply only to calls made through the matching interface, the `/v1/{account_id}/sales-navigator/...` and `/v1/{account_id}/recruiter/...` operations, and Curviate holds each call to the figure for the interface it goes through. The numbers here are therefore the ones a standard-interface call is held to, on every profile; a call through one of those operations resolves from the elevated set instead, and each row publishes that figure as `interface_ceiling`.

limit_profile_source.description: Where `limit_profile` came from. `detected`: Curviate read it from LinkedIn, at `limit_profile_detected_at`. `operator`: it was set through this operation and holds until you release it by sending `limit_profile_source: "default"` on this operation, on its own (changing `limit_profile` and releasing it in the same request is refused). Nothing else overrides it: a connect, a reconnect and an account read all leave a pinned value exactly as you set it. `default`: it has never been observed, so the value is the seeded `basic` and says nothing about the account; Curviate detects it on the account's next read or connect.

limit_profile_detected_at.description: When Curviate last read `limit_profile` from LinkedIn, whether or not the value changed. Null until it has. Curviate re-reads it on connect and, at most once a day, on an account read, so a subscription change reaches the numbers without a reconnect. While `limit_profile_source` is `operator` neither the value nor this timestamp moves, until you release the pin.

warm_up.description: The account's ACTIVE warm-up, derived on every read. While warm-up holds an account back, every row's effective ceiling is its configured ceiling multiplied by `factor`, so a `factor` of 0.15 means the account is held to 15 percent of the numbers the rows report. Only `enabled` is settable (PATCH with `warm_up: {enabled}`); the other keys are derived, and sent back on a write they are accepted and ignored. This is separate from the per-row `warm_up_state` and `warm_up_factor`, which report what is active on that row: set `warm_up_factor` on a row to override the ramps (recovery after a restriction still caps it). Every warm-up number is inferred; none is published by LinkedIn. Curviate infers no account age.

enabled.description: The account's warm-up switch, default true. Off skips the connect ramp and the quiet ramp; recovery after a LinkedIn restriction still applies. Set it with PATCH /v1/{account_id}/safety-policy and `warm_up: {enabled}`, or with `warm_up` at connect.

state.description: `none` is an account at full speed. `ramping` is an account climbing 0.15, 0.35, 0.60, 0.85 to 1.00 by week after its connect or after a quiet spell. `restriction_recovery` is an account under, or just out of, a LinkedIn restriction: it holds at 0 for seven days after the restriction lifts, resumes at 0.40, then steps up 0.15 every four days.

factor.description: The multiplier applied to every row's ceiling: the lowest of every applying trigger's. 1 is not ramping.

week.description: Which week of the ramp supplies `factor`, counted from the connect or the return from a quiet spell, whichever is later. Null when no ramp applies or restriction recovery is lower.

steps.description: How many weeks the ramp has (5 today: 0.15, 0.35, 0.60, 0.85, 1.00). Read with `week` (0-based): week 1 is the second of `steps`.

triggers.description: The triggers that apply now: `connect` in the first 28 days after connect, `dormant` after more than 30 days with no action (counted from the connect when the account never acted) until the ramp it started completes, `post_restriction` under or recovering from a LinkedIn restriction. With warm-up off only `post_restriction` can apply.

dormant.description: True when the account has had no action for over 30 days (counted from its connect when it never acted), whether warm-up is on or off. With warm-up on, its next action starts the ramp at 0.15.

activity_window.description: The zone the activity window is read in, derived from where the account connects. Outside the window, a live write to LinkedIn is refused; reads and anything served from Curviate's own store are never affected, at any hour. Read-only: a write accepts it back and ignores it, so a read policy can be sent back unchanged.

effective_timezone.description: The IANA zone the activity window is read in, from where the account connects (its Curviate proxy's country, or your own proxy's detected location). Nobody sets it. Null while the zone is unknown: see fallback_timezones.

source.description: Where the zone came from: country (the connection country), region (a chosen region inside it), detected (a check of the proxy's location), or none (nothing yet).

zone_state.description: known: one zone. pinned: one zone a check agreed on, kept until the next location change. unknown: the account acts only in hours every zone in fallback_timezones shares; with none, it does not act until Curviate can tell where it connects from.

fallback_timezones.description: The candidate zones while zone_state is unknown, empty otherwise. Empty while unknown means the window is closed.

active_hours.description: This account's active hours in force for an action type with no edges of its own: its own `active_hours` when set (source `account`), else the Team's (`team`), else Curviate's default, Monday to Friday 07:00 to 22:00 (`default`). Set it here; null falls back to the Team's. Live writes happen only on these days, between start and end, in each account's own time zone; each edge varies by up to 45 minutes a day. Write `{days, start, end}` (at least one day, start and end different, an end before the start wraps past midnight) or null to clear; no days, equal edges, an unknown day or a time that is not HH:MM is a 400. `source` is read-only: sending the read back changes nothing.

days.description: The active days, in week order.

source.description: Where these hours come from: `account`, `team` or `default`.

budget_row.description: The counted-action row this policy governs.

ceiling.description: What this row refuses at (limits are always enforced), in the row's own unit. Null means the row is uncalibrated: Curviate has no figure for it.

window_kind.description: The calendar grain this row is counted in.

window_span.description: How many grain units one counting window spans.

window_timezone.description: IANA zone name the counting window is aligned to. Null counts in UTC.

activity_window_start.description: Local HH:MM this row's activity window opens: the hours in force, from the rung `activity_window_source` names.

activity_window_end.description: Local HH:MM this row's activity window closes, from the same rung.

activity_window_source.description: Where this row's hours come from, the first rung that is set: `account_row` (this row's own edges on the account), `account` (the account's `active_hours`), `team_row` (the Team's row default), `team` (the Team's `active_hours`) or `default` (07:00 to 22:00). Read-only. A row's own edges never change the days: those are the `active_hours` below it.

activity_window_applies_to.description: What the activity window governs. `writes` (the default) covers live writes to LinkedIn; `all` widens it to live reads as well, which is the setting for a persona that should not be seen browsing at 03:00. It is broader than it sounds: `all` covers every live read, including the ones about the account itself, so a nightly analytics or invitation-backlog poll is refused at 03:00 too. A read Curviate answers from its own store never reaches LinkedIn, so it is never subject to the window under either setting, at any hour; the same read IS covered when the store cannot answer it, or when you ask for it live. Inbound events are never subject to it either. One action set to `all` reaches the whole account's live reads that spend no budget of their own (notifications, profile analytics, SSI, profile visitors, the invitation and saved-list listings): those calls debit no action type, so they have none to read this setting from and take the account-wide answer instead. Reads that DO debit an action type read that action type's own setting.

warm_up_state.description: The warm-up state ACTIVE on this row: the label for `warm_up_factor` beside it, so the two always agree. Read-only, so a value sent on a write is accepted and ignored; set `warm_up_factor` to pin this row's ramp.

warm_up_factor.description: The multiplier ACTIVE on this row, which is what `effective_ceiling` above was computed with. 1 is not ramping. Set it to pin this row and ignore the account's derived ramps; leave it unset to follow the derivation. Recovery after a LinkedIn restriction still caps it: while the account recovers, the lower of the two applies.

character_cap.description: Length cap on the row's free-text field, in characters.

subject_character_cap.description: Length cap on the row's subject line, in characters.

per_query_cap.description: Bound on a single query's result lines. Search rows only.

source_class.description: How well calibrated this row's number is. `unseeded` means Curviate has no green, amber or ceiling figure for this row on this profile: the row is reported so nothing is silently missing, but nothing has calibrated it, so no value you set can be `over_default`.

effective_ceiling.description: What this row is ACTUALLY held to right now: `ceiling` with the account's warm-up ramp applied. Read this one, not `ceiling`, to know where the next call will be stopped. On an account in warm-up the two differ, and in the first week after connect they differ by a factor of about seven. Null when the row has no ceiling to ramp. `warm_up_state` and `warm_up_factor` beside it are the values ACTIVE on this row, not the seeded ones.

interface_ceiling.description: What a call through the matching ELEVATED interface is held to on this row: the `/v1/{account_id}/sales-navigator/...` and `/v1/{account_id}/recruiter/...` operations. Null when this row and limit profile have no such figure, which is every row on `basic` and `premium` and most rows everywhere. Everything else on this row (`ceiling`, `effective_ceiling`, `band` and `over_default`) is the STANDARD-interface figure, because one counter serves both interfaces and the standard side is the conservative one to band against. The consequence is worth reading: on a `sales_navigator` or `recruiter` account a row can report `band: "over"` with `posture: "enforce"` while a call through the elevated interface still succeeds; the refusal the band predicts is the one a standard call gets.

effective_interface_ceiling.description: `interface_ceiling` with the account's warm-up ramp applied, and null wherever `interface_ceiling` is null. Read THIS to know where an elevated-interface call stops, for the same reason `effective_ceiling` rather than `ceiling` answers that for a standard one.

items.description: One configured value that exceeds Curviate's own seeded default. Present for as long as the value is above default; there is no acknowledgement that clears it. Setting the value back to the default removes it.

field.description: The field whose configured value is above default.

source_class.description: How well calibrated the DEFAULT is. `substrate` and `linkedin_official` are published figures; `practitioner` is corroborated operator experience; `inferred` is our own reasoning; `unseeded` means we have no figure at all for that row, in which case there is nothing to be above and no entry appears. over_default.description: Empty when nothing on this row is above default. Computed against the STANDARD-interface default, like `band` and for the same reason.

pacing.description: How Curviate paces Motion actions on this account: before a Motion action of a type, at least `min_gap_seconds` plus a random part of `jitter_seconds` must have passed since the account's previous Motion action of that type, and `global.min_gap_seconds` since its previous Motion action of any type or its previous LinkedIn write through the API. `read` covers profile and post reads. Write any subset as `pacing: {"invite.send": {"min_gap_seconds": 600}}`; null clears a field or a whole type back to the default. Values are whole seconds from 0 to 86400 and are never clamped; an unknown type or field, a fraction or an out-of-range value is a 400 naming it.

jitter_seconds.description: A random extra of up to this many seconds added to each gap. Absent on `global`, which has no jitter.
