notices.description: Present on a write only, and only when it sent a removed key (`posture`, `tenant_default_posture`): one POSTURE_REMOVED entry per key, naming it and the last day it is accepted (2027-01-25). Nothing was stored for it. Branch on code, never on message.

code.description: The key was removed: limits are always enforced. Stop sending it.

field.description: The removed key the request sent.

message.description: What was removed and the last day it is accepted.

overDefault.summary: After raising a ceiling above the default

400.description: INVALID_REQUEST. The row name or source class is not one of the accepted values, `warm_up.enabled` is not a boolean, or a number is not a number (a negative ceiling). A value is never rejected for being unsafe: any limit may be set to any value, and a high one is reported rather than refused. A time zone is not a setting: any value but null in `timezone` or a row's `activity_window_timezone` is refused with "The time zone follows where this account connects from. Change it with PATCH /v1/accounts/{account_id} and `country`, or your own `proxy`." Null is accepted and ignored, so a document read before this change can be sent back once its zones are null. `posture` and `tenant_default_posture` were removed: limits are always enforced; to send more, raise the limit. Until 2027-01-25 (the last accepted day) the value "enforce" or null is still accepted, stores nothing and earns a POSTURE_REMOVED entry in `notices` plus a `Deprecation: true` header; "warn" on any day, or any value after that day, is refused with a message naming the key. TEAM_REQUIRED: an All-Teams key sent no X-Curviate-Team header (on an account route: with an account id that is not one); GET /v1/teams lists your teams.

value.message: A parameter failed validation.
Name the Team with the X-Curviate-Team header. GET /v1/teams lists yours.

404.description: No such account for this tenant. An id whose connection was replaced or removed also stops resolving here, and it is already absent from the list, so re-read `GET /v1/accounts` for the current id.

value.message: The referenced resource does not exist for this tenant.

413.description: Payload too large, the request body exceeds the size limit.

value.message: Request body is too large: it exceeds the 9437184-byte limit.

429.description: Rate limited, slow down and retry after the hinted delay.

value.message: The per-account request rate limit was exceeded; retry after the delay in retry_hint. Per-team breaches carry RATE_LIMIT_TENANT; ingress-wide breaches (pre-auth, no per-client key) and upstream saturation both carry PLATFORM_RATE_LIMIT. A 429 on a budgeted action can also be BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, which is Curviate's own account-safety ceiling rather than a request-rate limit: it never reached LinkedIn, spent nothing, and carries row, reset_at and hint.

patch.description: Updates this account's safety policy. Send only the fields you're changing; null clears an override back to the tenant or Curviate default. Any value is accepted, none are clamped. Limits are always enforced: to send more, raise the limit. Fields and precedence: /reference/safety.

limit_profile.description: Which set of Curviate defaults this account's rows resolve from: `basic`, `premium`, `sales_navigator` or `recruiter`. Each inherits the one before it and raises a few rows. This is the platform product active on the account, NOT the Curviate seat entitlement, and the two can disagree: a lapsed subscription leaves the seat untouched. Curviate detects it from the platform when the account connects, re-detects it on every reconnect and, at most once a day, on an account read; setting it here pins it, and the pin wins over detection from then on. None of those paths moves a pinned value, so it holds until you release it. To release the pin, send `limit_profile_source: "default"` on its own: Curviate re-reads the value from LinkedIn on the account's next read or connect. Changing `limit_profile` and releasing it in the same request is refused with `INVALID_REQUEST`, because those are opposite intents. Sending the value the account already holds changes nothing and pins nothing. The change is recorded in the ledger and it moves the defaults under every row at once, so any row you have configured explicitly keeps your value. The elevated Sales Navigator and Recruiter figures apply only to calls made through the matching interface, the Sales Navigator and Recruiter operations, and Curviate holds each call to the figure for the interface it goes through. The numbers here are therefore the ones a standard-interface call is held to, on every profile; a call through one of those operations resolves from the elevated set instead, and each row publishes that figure as `interface_ceiling`.

timezone.description: Not a setting: the time zone follows where this account connects from (activity_window shows it). Any value but null is a 400 INVALID_REQUEST; change where the account connects instead (its `country`, or your own `proxy`). Null is accepted and ignored, so a document read before this change can be sent back once its zone is null.

tenant_default_posture.description: REMOVED: limits are always enforced; to send more, raise the limit. "enforce" (or null) is still accepted until 2027-01-25, changes nothing and earns a POSTURE_REMOVED notice; "warn", or any value after that day, is refused with INVALID_REQUEST.

clear_halts.description: Lift the platform pause on these action types now, instead of waiting for it to expire. When the platform refuses a call on an account (a rate limit, a server error on a budgeted route, an invitation resend cooldown), Curviate pauses that action type for the platform's own retry-after or a seeded cooldown, and every later call on it is refused locally without reaching the platform. Naming an action type here clears that pause: the next call goes out. Read `quotas[].halt` on the account to see which action types are paused and for how long. A type with no active pause is accepted and does nothing, so this is safe to send for a set you have not checked. Clearing is recorded in the account's ledger with the expiry it cut short, who cleared it and when, and it appears on the safety-events surface. It does not disarm anything: if the platform refuses the account again, the pause comes straight back, longer than the one you cleared where the platform says so. Clear a pause when you have reason to believe the refusal was a transient upstream fault rather than the platform pushing back on this account; clearing one and calling straight back into a real rate limit is itself how accounts get restricted.

posture.description: REMOVED: limits are always enforced; to send more, raise the limit. "enforce" (or null) is still accepted until 2027-01-25, changes nothing and earns a POSTURE_REMOVED notice; "warn", or any value after that day, is refused with INVALID_REQUEST.

budget_row.description: The budget row this patch configures.

ceiling.description: What this row refuses at, in this row's own unit: limits are always enforced. Any value up to 9007199254740991 is accepted and stored verbatim; a value above the Curviate default is reported back, never clamped.

green.description: Routine band. Activity at or below it is unremarkable.

amber.description: Warn-louder band, between green and the ceiling.

window_kind.description: The calendar grain this row is counted in.

window_span.description: How many `window_kind` units one counting window spans.

window_timezone.description: IANA zone name the counting window is aligned to, e.g. `Europe/Berlin` or `UTC`. Must be a real zone; anything else is a 400. Null counts in UTC.

posture.description: REMOVED: limits are always enforced; to send more, raise the limit. "enforce" (or null) is still accepted until 2027-01-25, changes nothing and earns a POSTURE_REMOVED notice; "warn", or any value after that day, is refused with INVALID_REQUEST.

activity_window_start.description: Local time the activity window opens, HH:MM. Outside the window, live write operations are refused.

activity_window_end.description: Local time the activity window closes, HH:MM. Must differ from activity_window_start (in force after the write); equal edges are a 400.

activity_window_timezone.description: Not a setting: the time zone follows where this account connects from (activity_window on the policy shows it). Any value but null is a 400 INVALID_REQUEST; change where the account connects instead (its `country`, or your own `proxy`). Null is accepted and ignored, so a row read before this change can be sent back once its zone is null.

activity_window_applies_to.description: What the activity window governs. `writes` (the default) covers live writes to LinkedIn; `all` widens it to live reads. A read Curviate answers from its own store never reaches LinkedIn and so is never covered; the same read IS covered when the store cannot answer it, or when you ask for it live. Stored reads and inbound events are never subject to the window under either setting, at any hour. One action set to `all` reaches the whole account's live reads that spend no budget of their own (notifications, profile analytics, SSI, profile visitors, the invitation and saved-list listings): those calls debit no action type, so they have none to read this setting from and take the account-wide answer instead. Reads that DO debit an action type read that action type's own setting.

warm_up_state.description: READ-ONLY. The warm-up ramp state active on this row: the label for `warm_up_factor` beside it, derived from it, so the two always agree. A value sent here is still checked for being a state at all, and is then accepted and ignored: it is never stored and never recorded in the ledger. Set `warm_up_factor` to pin a row out of the ramp Curviate derives for the account.

warm_up_factor.description: Multiplier applied to this row's ceiling while ramping. 1 is not ramping.

character_cap.description: Length cap on this row's free-text field, in characters (an invitation note, an InMail body).

subject_character_cap.description: Length cap on this row's subject line, in characters.

per_query_cap.description: Bound on a single query's result lines. Search rows only.

source_class.description: How well calibrated this row's configured number is. Overriding it labels your own figure; the over-default warning always reports the class of the Curviate default.

effective_ceiling.description: READ-ONLY. `ceiling` with the account's warm-up ramp applied, which is what this row is actually held to. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

interface_ceiling.description: READ-ONLY. What a call through the matching elevated interface (the Sales Navigator and Recruiter operations) is held to on this row, or null when this row and limit profile have no such figure. `ceiling`, `effective_ceiling`, `band` and `over_default` are all the STANDARD-interface figure, so on a `sales_navigator` or `recruiter` account a row can report `over` while a call through the elevated interface still succeeds. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

effective_interface_ceiling.description: READ-ONLY. `interface_ceiling` with the account's warm-up ramp applied. Read THIS to know where an elevated-interface call stops, for the same reason `effective_ceiling` and not `ceiling` answers that for a standard one. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

posture_source.description: REMOVED from the read (SF-04). Accepted and ignored until 2027-01-25 so an older document round-trips; refused after.

over_default.description: READ-ONLY. The fields on this row configured above the Curviate default. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

activity_window_source.description: Read-only, ignored: the rung this row's hours come from.

rows.description: Per-row configuration. Each entry names its `budget_row` and the fields to change. A row read back from the policy document may be sent here unchanged: its read-only fields (`effective_ceiling`, `over_default`, `warm_up_state`) are accepted and ignored.

min_gap_seconds.description: Whole seconds, 0 to 86400. Null clears it.

jitter_seconds.description: Whole seconds, 0 to 86400. Not on `global`. Null clears it.

over_default.description: READ-ONLY. The over-default warnings (a value below the default). Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

pacing.description: Motion pacing at this scope (an account, or the team default every account inherits), keyed by action type (`invite.send`, `post.comment`, `message.send`, `inmail.send`, `profile.follow`, `profile.unfollow`, `skill.endorse`, `invite.withdraw`, `post.react`), `read` and `global`: `{"invite.send": {"min_gap_seconds": 600, "jitter_seconds": 360}}`. Any subset; null clears a field or a type back to the default. Whole seconds from 0 to 86400, never clamped. A value below the default carries an `over_default` warning, the rows' own shape. Direct API calls are never paced.

end.description: Local HH:MM, not equal to start; before start wraps midnight.

source.description: Read-only, ignored.

active_hours.description: This account's own active hours: the days and local hours live writes happen in. Null falls back to the Team default. A row's own activity_window_start/end win over it, keeping these days. The read reports the hours in force and their source; sent back, it changes nothing.

object.description: READ-ONLY. The document's type discriminator. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

account_id.description: READ-ONLY. The account this document describes; the path names it. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

limit_profile_source.description: Where `limit_profile` came from: `default` (never observed), `detected` (read from LinkedIn) or `operator` (pinned through this operation, and nothing but a release moves it). Sending `default` releases a pin: the value is re-read from LinkedIn on the account's next read or connect. Send it on its own; changing `limit_profile` in the same request is refused. Sending `detected` or `operator` is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips.

limit_profile_detected_at.description: READ-ONLY. When `limit_profile` was last read from LinkedIn, or null if it never has been. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

posture_source.description: REMOVED from the read (SF-04). Accepted and ignored until 2027-01-25 so an older document round-trips; refused after.

enabled.description: Turn this account's warm-up on (true, the default) or off (false). Off skips the connect ramp and the quiet ramp; recovery after a LinkedIn restriction still applies.

warm_up.description: The account's warm-up. Only `enabled` is settable; its other keys are derived on every read, accepted and ignored, so the read's object can be sent back unchanged.

activity_window.description: Read-only: the time zone the activity window is read in, from where this account connects. Accepted and ignored, so the read's object can be sent back unchanged. The window's settable inputs are per row: `activity_window_start`, `activity_window_end`, `activity_window_applies_to`.

raiseCeiling.summary: Raise one row's ceiling far above the default

tightenOneRow.summary: Lower one row's ceiling, leaving every other field untouched

limitProfile.summary: Move the account onto the Sales Navigator defaults

activityWindowAll.summary: Hold live READS to the window too, not only writes

warmUpOff.summary: Turn this account's warm-up off (recovery after a restriction still applies)

clearHalt.summary: Lift the platform pause on one action type now, instead of waiting it out

activityWindowHours.summary: Narrow one row's activity window to office hours

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: The account ID (`acc_...`) whose safety events to read.

parameters.name: X-Curviate-Team
parameters.description: The team id to act in (GET /v1/teams lists yours). Required with an All-Teams key, except on account routes. A team key accepts only its own team.

parameters.name: Curviate-Client
parameters.description: Informational: which Curviate client sent the call (`sdk/<version>`, `cli/<version>`). It only feeds the dashboard's Integrations status lines and changes nothing about the request. The SDK and CLI send it for you.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response; decodable, pass it back verbatim.

parameters.name: budget_row
parameters.description: Return only events flagged against this budget row. Omit for every row.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only events at or after this instant (ISO-8601, e.g. 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z).

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Only events strictly before this instant (ISO-8601).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many events to return per page, 1 to 100. Defaults to 50.

200.description: What Curviate refused on this account (warned: past entries only, recorded before limits were always enforced), newest first. Filter by `budget_row` to ask about one action type, and by `since` / `until` to ask about a period.

id.description: The event's id. Also the value encoded in the next page's cursor.

budget_row.description: The budget row that breached. It is not always a row the call itself spends: an invitation refused because the outstanding backlog is at its ceiling reports `pending_invites`, which is the thing that breached. `*` means the event was not about a row at all: the activity window closing on an action that spends no budget of its own, such as editing a message or a Recruiter admin action. The `budget_row` filter accepts real row names only, so page without it to see those.

reason.description: Which rule flagged it, and each one calls for a different response. `budget_exhausted`: the account reached the ceiling configured for that row, which you can raise on the safety policy. `activity_window`: the account was acting outside its configured activity window, so no ceiling was the constraint. Wait for the window to open (`reset_at`), or change the setting `hint.parameter` names: `active_hours`, or a row's `activity_window_start` or `activity_window_end`. `rate_limited`: the platform itself refused this account on that row recently and Curviate is holding the row until the pause expires. No ceiling you raise lifts it; the one thing that does is `clear_halts` on the safety policy, which lifts it deliberately and records that it was lifted. `halt_cleared` is the odd one out and the only entry that is not a refusal: somebody lifted one of those platform pauses early through `clear_halts` on the safety policy, so the row was open again from that instant. It carries `blocked: false` and its `method` is `update_safety_policy` rather than the operation that breached. Read it beside the `rate_limited` entry it lifts: the pause and its lifting are one thread, and an entry list that showed only the first would report a row as still paused.

blocked.description: Whether the action was stopped. Limits are always enforced, so every new limit hit is `true`. `false` appears on two kinds of entry: a `halt_cleared` record, which stopped nothing but lifted a stop, and warnings recorded before limits were always enforced, kept as history.

method.description: The operation the caller was running when it breached.

items.description: Flagged events, newest first. [] when this account has never breached a limit.

cursor.description: Cursor for the next page; null on the terminal page. Pass it back verbatim. Page until cursor is null.

default.summary: Three refusals, one per rule, an operator lifting an earlier platform pause, and a warning kept from before limits were always enforced

empty.summary: Nothing has been flagged on this account

400.description: Invalid request: an out-of-range `limit`, an unknown `budget_row`, a malformed `since` / `until`, or a corrupt `cursor`. TEAM_REQUIRED: an All-Teams key sent no X-Curviate-Team header (on an account route: with an account id that is not one); GET /v1/teams lists your teams.

value.message: A parameter failed validation.
Name the Team with the X-Curviate-Team header. GET /v1/teams lists yours.

404.description: No such account for this tenant. An id whose connection was replaced or removed also stops resolving here, and it is already absent from the list, so re-read `GET /v1/accounts` for the current id.

value.message: The referenced resource does not exist for this tenant.

429.description: Rate limited, slow down and retry after the hinted delay.

value.message: The per-account request rate limit was exceeded; retry after the delay in retry_hint. Per-team breaches carry RATE_LIMIT_TENANT; ingress-wide breaches (pre-auth, no per-client key) and upstream saturation both carry PLATFORM_RATE_LIMIT. A 429 on a budgeted action can also be BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, which is Curviate's own account-safety ceiling rather than a request-rate limit: it never reached LinkedIn, spent nothing, and carries row, reset_at and hint.

get.description: Each entry is an action Curviate refused at a safety limit or pause, or a halt_cleared record of a pause lifted early (blocked false; so are pre-enforcement warnings). Filter by budget_row, since and until; page until cursor is null.

parameters.name: X-Curviate-Team
parameters.description: The team id to act in (GET /v1/teams lists yours). Required with an All-Teams key, except on account routes. A team key accepts only its own team.

parameters.name: Curviate-Client
parameters.description: Informational: which Curviate client sent the call (`sdk/<version>`, `cli/<version>`). It only feeds the dashboard's Integrations status lines and changes nothing about the request. The SDK and CLI send it for you.

200.description: The tenant safety defaults, every limit profile and every budget row.

active_hours.description: The Team default active hours every account without its own uses: the Team's `active_hours` when set (source `team`), else Curviate's default, Monday to Friday 07:00 to 22:00 (`default`). A Team created from 2026-10 on starts with the same, set on the Team. Live writes happen only on these days, between start and end, in each account's own time zone; each edge varies by up to 45 minutes a day. Write `{days, start, end}` (at least one day, start and end different, an end before the start wraps past midnight) or null to clear; no days, equal edges, an unknown day or a time that is not HH:MM is a 400. `source` is read-only: sending the read back changes nothing.

days.description: The active days, in week order.

source.description: Where these hours come from: `account`, `team` or `default`.

profiles.description: One entry per limit profile, always all of them.

limit_profile.description: The limit profile these defaults apply to. An account resolves from its own profile's defaults.

budget_row.description: The counted-action row this policy governs.

ceiling.description: What this row refuses at (limits are always enforced), in the row's own unit. Null means the row is uncalibrated: Curviate has no figure for it.

window_kind.description: The calendar grain this row is counted in.

window_span.description: How many grain units one counting window spans.

window_timezone.description: IANA zone name the counting window is aligned to. Null counts in UTC.

activity_window_start.description: Local HH:MM this row's activity window opens: the hours in force, from the rung `activity_window_source` names.

activity_window_end.description: Local HH:MM this row's activity window closes, from the same rung.

activity_window_source.description: Where this row's hours come from, the first rung that is set: `account_row` (this row's own edges on the account), `account` (the account's `active_hours`), `team_row` (the Team's row default), `team` (the Team's `active_hours`) or `default` (07:00 to 22:00). Read-only. A row's own edges never change the days: those are the `active_hours` below it.

activity_window_applies_to.description: What the activity window governs. `writes` (the default) covers live writes to LinkedIn; `all` widens it to live reads as well, which is the setting for a persona that should not be seen browsing at 03:00. It is broader than it sounds: `all` covers every live read, including the ones about the account itself, so a nightly analytics or invitation-backlog poll is refused at 03:00 too. A read Curviate answers from its own store never reaches LinkedIn, so it is never subject to the window under either setting, at any hour; the same read IS covered when the store cannot answer it, or when you ask for it live. Inbound events are never subject to it either. One action set to `all` reaches the whole account's live reads that spend no budget of their own (notifications, profile analytics, SSI, profile visitors, the invitation and saved-list listings): those calls debit no action type, so they have none to read this setting from and take the account-wide answer instead. Reads that DO debit an action type read that action type's own setting.

warm_up_factor.description: The tenant default multiplier for this row, or null when none is set. Null means each account follows its own derived warm-up ramp; 1 pins every account on this profile out of it.

character_cap.description: Length cap on the row's free-text field, in characters.

subject_character_cap.description: Length cap on the row's subject line, in characters.

per_query_cap.description: Bound on a single query's result lines. Search rows only.

source_class.description: How well calibrated this row's number is. `unseeded` means Curviate has no green, amber or ceiling figure for this row on this profile: the row is reported so nothing is silently missing, but nothing has calibrated it, so no value you set can be `over_default`.

interface_ceiling.description: What a call through the matching ELEVATED interface is held to on this row: the `/v1/{account_id}/sales-navigator/...` and `/v1/{account_id}/recruiter/...` operations. Null when this row and limit profile have no such figure, which is every row on `basic` and `premium` and most rows everywhere. Everything else on this row (`ceiling`, `effective_ceiling`, `band` and `over_default`) is the STANDARD-interface figure, because one counter serves both interfaces and the standard side is the conservative one to band against. The consequence is worth reading: on a `sales_navigator` or `recruiter` account a row can report `band: "over"` with `posture: "enforce"` while a call through the elevated interface still succeeds; the refusal the band predicts is the one a standard call gets.

items.description: One configured value that exceeds Curviate's own seeded default. Present for as long as the value is above default; there is no acknowledgement that clears it. Setting the value back to the default removes it.

field.description: The field whose configured value is above default.

source_class.description: How well calibrated the DEFAULT is. `substrate` and `linkedin_official` are published figures; `practitioner` is corroborated operator experience; `inferred` is our own reasoning; `unseeded` means we have no figure at all for that row, in which case there is nothing to be above and no entry appears. Read this before deciding whether being above default matters.

over_default.description: Empty when nothing on this row is above default. Computed against the STANDARD-interface default, like `band` and for the same reason.

rows.description: Every budget row, always: the tenant default where one is set, the Curviate default otherwise.

pacing.description: The team's Motion pacing defaults: the Curviate default where the team has set nothing. Every account inherits them unless it sets its own. How Curviate paces Motion actions on this account: before a Motion action of a type, at least `min_gap_seconds` plus a random part of `jitter_seconds` must have passed since the account's previous Motion action of that type, and `global.min_gap_seconds` since its previous Motion action of any type or its previous LinkedIn write through the API. `read` covers profile and post reads. Direct API calls are never paced: those are yours to pace. Values resolve per field from Curviate's default, then the team's, then this account's. Write any subset as `pacing: {"invite.send": {"min_gap_seconds": 600}}`; null clears a field or a whole type back to the default. Values are whole seconds from 0 to 86400 and are never clamped; an unknown type or field, a fraction or an out-of-range value is a 400 naming it.

min_gap_seconds.description: The least time between two Motion calls of this type on the account, in seconds.

jitter_seconds.description: A random extra of up to this many seconds added to each gap. Absent on `global`, which has no jitter.

items.description: One pacing value set BELOW Curviate's default: a shorter gap paces the account more aggressively. The rows' own warning shape.

field.description: The pacing field set below default.

active_hours.description: The Team default active hours every account without its own uses: the Team's `active_hours` when set (source `team`), else Curviate's default, Monday to Friday 07:00 to 22:00 (`default`). A Team created from 2026-10 on starts with the same, set on the Team. Live writes happen only on these days, between start and end, in each account's own time zone; each edge varies by up to 45 minutes a day. Write `{days, start, end}` (at least one day, start and end different, an end before the start wraps past midnight) or null to clear; no days, equal edges, an unknown day or a time that is not HH:MM is a 400. `source` is read-only: sending the read back changes nothing.

activity_window_source.description: Where this row's hours come from, the first rung that is set: `account_row` (this row's own edges on the account), `account` (the account's `active_hours`), `team_row` (the Team's row default), `team` (the Team's `active_hours`) or `default` (07:00 to 22:00). Read-only. A row's own edges never change the days: those are the `active_hours` below it.

activity_window_applies_to.description: What the activity window governs. `writes` (the default) covers live writes to LinkedIn; `all` widens it to live reads as well, which is the setting for a persona that should not be seen browsing at 03:00. It is broader than it sounds: `all` covers every live read, including the ones about the account itself, so a nightly analytics or invitation-backlog poll is refused at 03:00 too. A read Curviate answers from its own store never reaches LinkedIn, so it is never subject to the window under either setting, at any hour; the same read IS covered when the store cannot answer it, or when you ask for it live. Inbound events are never subject to it either. One action set to `all` reaches the whole account's live reads that spend no budget of their own (notifications, profile analytics, SSI, profile visitors, the invitation and saved-list listings): those calls debit no action type, so they have none to read this setting from and take the account-wide answer instead. Reads that DO debit an action type read that action type's own setting.

warm_up_factor.description: The tenant default multiplier for this row, or null when none is set. Null means each account follows its own derived warm-up ramp; 1 pins every account on this profile out of it.

source_class.description: How well calibrated this row's number is. `unseeded` means Curviate has no green, amber or ceiling figure for this row on this profile: the row is reported so nothing is silently missing, but nothing has calibrated it, so no value you set can be `over_default`.

interface_ceiling.description: What a call through the matching ELEVATED interface is held to on this row: the `/v1/{account_id}/sales-navigator/...` and `/v1/{account_id}/recruiter/...` operations. Null when this row and limit profile have no such figure, which is every row on `basic` and `premium` and most rows everywhere. Everything else on this row (`ceiling`, `effective_ceiling`, `band` and `over_default`) is the STANDARD-interface figure, because one counter serves both interfaces and the standard side is the conservative one to band against. The consequence is worth reading: on a `sales_navigator` or `recruiter` account a row can report `band: "over"` with `posture: "enforce"` while a call through the elevated interface still succeeds; the refusal the band predicts is the one a standard call gets.

pacing.description: The team's Motion pacing defaults: the Curviate default where the team has set nothing. Every account inherits them unless it sets its own. How Curviate paces Motion actions on this account: before a Motion action of a type, at least `min_gap_seconds` plus a random part of `jitter_seconds` must have passed since the account's previous Motion action of that type, and `global.min_gap_seconds` since its previous Motion action of any type or its previous LinkedIn write through the API. `read` covers profile and post reads. Direct API calls are never paced: those are yours to pace. Values resolve per field from Curviate's default, then the team's, then this account's. Write any subset as `pacing: {"invite.send": {"min_gap_seconds": 600}}`; null clears a field or a whole type back to the default. Values are whole seconds from 0 to 86400 and are never clamped; an unknown type or field, a fraction or an out-of-range value is a 400 naming it.

400.description: INVALID_REQUEST. An unknown limit profile, row name or field, or a value that is not a value (a negative ceiling). A value is never rejected for being unsafe. A time zone is not a setting: any value but null in a row's `activity_window_timezone` is refused with "The time zone follows where this account connects from. Change it with PATCH /v1/accounts/{account_id} and `country`, or your own `proxy`." Null there is accepted and ignored. A top-level `timezone` is not a field of this operation: it is refused as an unknown key, null included. `posture` and `tenant_default_posture` were removed: limits are always enforced; to send more, raise the limit. Until 2027-01-25 (the last accepted day) the value "enforce" or null is still accepted, stores nothing and earns a POSTURE_REMOVED entry in `notices` plus a `Deprecation: true` header; "warn" on any day, or any value after that day, is refused with a message naming the key. TEAM_REQUIRED: an All-Teams key sent no X-Curviate-Team header (on an account route: with an account id that is not one); GET /v1/teams lists your teams.

value.message: The per-account request rate limit was exceeded; retry after the delay in retry_hint. Per-team breaches carry RATE_LIMIT_TENANT; ingress-wide breaches (pre-auth, no per-client key) and upstream saturation both carry PLATFORM_RATE_LIMIT. A 429 on a budgeted action can also be BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, which is Curviate's own account-safety ceiling rather than a request-rate limit: it never reached LinkedIn, spent nothing, and carries row, reset_at and hint.

patch.description: Updates tenant-wide safety defaults per limit profile and budget row; affects every account that hasn't overridden the field, immediately. Limits are always enforced. Fields and precedence: /reference/safety.

tenant_default_posture.description: REMOVED: limits are always enforced; to send more, raise the limit. "enforce" (or null) is still accepted until 2027-01-25, changes nothing and earns a POSTURE_REMOVED notice; "warn", or any value after that day, is refused with INVALID_REQUEST.

limit_profile.description: The limit profile these defaults apply to. An account resolves from the defaults of its own `limit_profile` only.

budget_row.description: The budget row this patch configures.

ceiling.description: What this row refuses at, in this row's own unit: limits are always enforced. Any value up to 9007199254740991 is accepted and stored verbatim; a value above the Curviate default is reported back, never clamped.

green.description: Routine band. Activity at or below it is unremarkable.

amber.description: Warn-louder band, between green and the ceiling.

window_kind.description: The calendar grain this row is counted in.

window_span.description: How many `window_kind` units one counting window spans.

window_timezone.description: IANA zone name the counting window is aligned to, e.g. `Europe/Berlin` or `UTC`. Must be a real zone; anything else is a 400. Null counts in UTC.

activity_window_start.description: Local time the activity window opens, HH:MM. Outside the window, live write operations are refused.

activity_window_end.description: Local time the activity window closes, HH:MM. Must differ from activity_window_start (in force after the write); equal edges are a 400.

activity_window_timezone.description: Not a setting: the time zone follows where this account connects from (activity_window on the policy shows it). Any value but null is a 400 INVALID_REQUEST; change where the account connects instead (its `country`, or your own `proxy`). Null is accepted and ignored, so a row read before this change can be sent back once its zone is null.

activity_window_applies_to.description: What the activity window governs. `writes` (the default) covers live writes to LinkedIn; `all` widens it to live reads. A read Curviate answers from its own store never reaches LinkedIn and so is never covered; the same read IS covered when the store cannot answer it, or when you ask for it live. Stored reads and inbound events are never subject to the window under either setting, at any hour. One action set to `all` reaches the whole account's live reads that spend no budget of their own (notifications, profile analytics, SSI, profile visitors, the invitation and saved-list listings): those calls debit no action type, so they have none to read this setting from and take the account-wide answer instead. Reads that DO debit an action type read that action type's own setting.

warm_up_factor.description: Multiplier applied to this row's ceiling while ramping. 1 is not ramping.

character_cap.description: Length cap on this row's free-text field, in characters (an invitation note, an InMail body).

subject_character_cap.description: Length cap on this row's subject line, in characters.

per_query_cap.description: Bound on a single query's result lines. Search rows only.

source_class.description: How well calibrated this row's configured number is. Overriding it labels your own figure; the over-default warning always reports the class of the Curviate default.

interface_ceiling.description: READ-ONLY. What a call through the matching elevated interface (the Sales Navigator and Recruiter operations) is held to on this row, or null when this row and limit profile have no such figure. `ceiling`, `effective_ceiling`, `band` and `over_default` are all the STANDARD-interface figure, so on a `sales_navigator` or `recruiter` account a row can report `over` while a call through the elevated interface still succeeds. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

over_default.description: READ-ONLY. The fields on this row configured above the Curviate default. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

activity_window_source.description: Read-only, ignored: the rung this row's hours come from.

rows.description: Per-row defaults for this profile. Omit a field to leave it; `null` clears the tenant default back to the Curviate default. A row read back from this document may be sent unchanged.

min_gap_seconds.description: Whole seconds, 0 to 86400. Null clears it.

jitter_seconds.description: Whole seconds, 0 to 86400. Not on `global`. Null clears it.

over_default.description: READ-ONLY. The over-default warnings (a value below the default). Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

pacing.description: Motion pacing at this scope (an account, or the team default every account inherits), keyed by action type (`invite.send`, `post.comment`, `message.send`, `inmail.send`, `profile.follow`, `profile.unfollow`, `skill.endorse`, `invite.withdraw`, `post.react`), `read` and `global`: `{"invite.send": {"min_gap_seconds": 600, "jitter_seconds": 360}}`. Any subset; null clears a field or a type back to the default. Whole seconds from 0 to 86400, never clamped. A value below the default carries an `over_default` warning, the rows' own shape. Direct API calls are never paced.

end.description: Local HH:MM, not equal to start; before start wraps midnight.

source.description: Read-only, ignored.

active_hours.description: The Team default active hours: the days and local hours live writes happen in. Null falls back to Curviate's default, 07:00-22:00 Monday to Friday. The read reports the hours in force and their source; sent back, it changes nothing.

object.description: READ-ONLY. The document's type discriminator. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

impact.description: READ-ONLY. What the last write changed across the tenant's accounts. Sent back on a write it is accepted and ignored, so the whole document round-trips; it is never stored and never ledgered.

parameters.name: id

parameters.name: X-Curviate-Team
parameters.description: The team id to act in (GET /v1/teams lists yours). Required with an All-Teams key, except on account routes. A team key accepts only its own team.

parameters.name: Curviate-Client
parameters.description: Informational: which Curviate client sent the call (`sdk/<version>`, `cli/<version>`). It only feeds the dashboard's Integrations status lines and changes nothing about the request. The SDK and CLI send it for you.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: How many Contacts to render, the first enrollable ones by list order. 1 to 20, default 5. Not with contact_ids.

parameters.name: contact_ids
parameters.description: Contact ids (con_...) to render, up to 20, in the order given. Not with sample. Repeat the key, comma-separate or mix; empties ignored.

200.description: The preview. Nothing is sent, nothing is saved and no budget is spent; whatever only LinkedIn can answer is unknown. Rendered text is shown here and never stored.

sequence_version.description: The Sequence version previewed.

paths.description: Every distinct route through the Sequence, from the first step and from on_reply, as step ids in order. A step that branched carries the exit taken (has_post:then). Every route ends with end.

truncated.description: true when there are more routes than the 200 listed, or when some rendered text was omitted (a response carries at most 1 MiB of it).

account_id.description: The sending account this Contact would be assigned, from stored data; null when none can act or assignment needs LinkedIn.

excluded.description: Why the Contact would not be enrolled, from stored data: the Team's do-not-contact list holds it, an Exclusion list holds it, it is or was within 90 days in another Motion, or an account already chats with it. null: nothing excludes it.

result.description: unknown: only LinkedIn can answer it.

steps.description: Every step that sends text, rendered for this Contact.

rendered.description: The text as it would go out; null when the fallback is drop or skip, or when omitted is true.

subject.description: The InMail subject; null otherwise, and when omitted is true.

omitted.description: true when the text exists but the response already carries 1 MiB of rendered text, so rendered and subject are null. used_fallback and would_skip are still judged.

used_fallback.description: true when a variable had no value or the text was over the account's length limit.

would_skip.description: A reason the step would be skipped that stored data settles (inmail_unavailable, missing_variable, text_too_long), else unknown.

projection.description: An estimate of how long the list takes, from each account's current budget ceilings (warm-up applied). Each Contact is enrolled on min(accounts_per_contact, accounts that can act) accounts; those Enrollments split evenly over the accounts. It ignores what other Motions spend.

audience.description: The Contacts of the source lists, counted from stored data (nothing is read from LinkedIn), each once. A Contact that would be skipped for several reasons counts under the first: do_not_contact, excluded, other_motion, known_chat, filtered. Present even when the Motion has no Sequence.

total.description: Contacts in the Motion's source lists, each counted once.

do_not_contact.description: On the Team's do-not-contact list. Always skipped, whatever the Motion's settings.

excluded.description: In one of the Motion's exclusion lists.

other_motion.description: In another Motion, or in one within the last 90 days, when settings.exclude.other_motions is on. Whatever that setting, a Contact deleted and imported again whose earlier record was already in this Motion counts here too.

known_chat.description: An account already chats with them (when settings.exclude.known_chats is on).

filtered.description: Fail a where filter on stored Contact data (fields, extra fields, tags). A filter only LinkedIn can answer, such as degree or premium, is checked when the Contact enrolls and does not count here.

to_enroll.description: total minus every skipped count: the Contacts the projection plans for.

contacts.description: Contacts the projection plans for: audience.to_enroll. null when the Motion has no Sequence.
This account's share of the Enrollments: with accounts_per_contact above 1, one Contact counts on each account it is enrolled on.

enroll_days.description: Schedule days to enroll that share; null when a ceiling of 0 admits none.

binding.description: The limit that set this account's pace: daily_cap, or a budget row such as connection_requests_no_note.

longest_path_days.description: Calendar days of waits and timeouts on the longest route, rounded up. null when the Motion has no Sequence.

finish_working_days.description: Schedule days until the last Contact finishes: the slowest account's enroll_days plus the longest route in schedule days, plus, with accounts_per_contact above 1, settings.account_gap (default 1d) in schedule days for each further account a Contact is enrolled on. null when nothing can run.

fits_before_end_at.description: Whether every Contact finishes before schedule.end_at, counting schedule days from now (or schedule.start_at if later). null when the schedule has no end_at or the Motion has no Sequence. schedule.hours is not modelled: the estimate assumes each day's actions fit the daily window.

binding.description: The slowest account and its limiter; null when no sending account can act.

summary.description: One line that says it is an estimate at the account's steady-state ceiling, for example: 100 Contacts finish in 27 working days; binding row daily_cap (an estimate at each Account's steady-state ceiling). 200.description: Enrollments, newest first. Filters combine with AND. The counted unit is the Enrollment, one Contact on one account in one Motion: each Contact counts once per Account. done_step with outcome lists who did what at a Step: executed, skipped, failed (the Step's own record; a condition or wait counts as executed); accepted, not_accepted (on invite.send: its invitation was accepted, or withdrawn or never accepted before the wait for it timed out; on an until invite.accepted: its then or else exit); replied, no_reply (on message.send or inmail.send: a reply came after it, or none and the Enrollment left the following until message.replied by else or finished; on an until message.replied: its then or else exit); seen (on message.send or inmail.send: a read receipt arrived for it or the person replied after it, the same rule as the analytics seen rate). parameters.description: Informational: which Curviate client sent the call (`sdk/<version>`, `cli/<version>`). It only feeds the dashboard's Integrations status lines and changes nothing about the request. The SDK and CLI send it for you.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day of the window, YYYY-MM-DD, read in timezone. Default: 29 days before to.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day of the window, inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD, read in timezone. Default: today (29 days after from when only from is set); a later day is clamped to today.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: 7d, 30d, 90d, 12m (same date a year back, 366 days across a 29 February) or all (since the Team was created). Not with from or to.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Groups daily: day, week (from Monday), month, or auto (day to 90 days, week to 366, month beyond). Default: auto with range, day with from/to.

parameters.name: timezone
parameters.description: IANA zone the days are read in, e.g. Europe/Berlin. Default: UTC.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: Only these accounts (acc_...). Default: every account you can see. Repeat the key, comma-separate or mix; empties ignored.

parameters.name: motion_id
parameters.description: Only these Motions (mot_...). Default: every Motion. Repeat the key, comma-separate or mix; empties ignored.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: motion, unibox (the Unibox), api (any API key or MCP grant), direct (unibox and api). Default: all. Repeat the key, comma-separate or mix; empties ignored.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Sections: performance, daily, motions, accounts, flags. Omitted: the summary. Repeat the key, comma-separate or mix; empties ignored.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Dotted paths kept in the sections, e.g. motions.reply.rate. A requested path always appears. Repeat the key, comma-separate or mix; empties ignored.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Orders lists: sent, acceptance.rate, reply.rate, inmail_reply.rate, last_activity_at, name. -key: desc. Repeat the key, comma-separate or mix; empties ignored.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per list section (motions, accounts), 1-100. Default: 5 in the summary, else every item.

parameters.name: compare
parameters.description: previous_period: each rate gains previous (the same number of days just before from) and delta (rate - previous rate).

200.description: Results across your Motions and direct actions (API, CLI, MCP, Unibox). Each Contact counts once per Account and source. totals counts every visible record, archived Motions included; motions lists every Motion but drafts (archived ones only with records in the window), latest activity first, at most 100 (motions_truncated). Lags: a step counts once it settles, a reply within a minute, an acceptance about 2 hours after it happens. Grammar: include picks the sections (performance is totals under its section name), fields keeps dotted paths, sort and limit order and cut motions and accounts, compare=previous_period adds previous and delta to every rate, flags lists what to look at, and every Motion, account and step row carries next, the exact CLI call. Once any of these is given and include is not, the body is the summary: performance, the lists' top 5 by sent, flags. With none of them the full body of before is returned with a Deprecation header; it becomes the summary later.

value.message: The per-account request rate limit was exceeded; retry after the delay in retry_hint. A 429 on a budgeted action can also be BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, which is Curviate's own account-safety ceiling rather than a request-rate limit: it never reached LinkedIn, spent nothing, and carries row, reset_at and hint.

parameters.name: motion_id
parameters.description: Motion id (mot_...).

parameters.name: X-Curviate-Team
parameters.description: The team id to act in (GET /v1/teams lists yours). Required with an All-Teams key, except on account routes. A team key accepts only its own team.

parameters.name: Curviate-Client
parameters.description: Informational: which Curviate client sent the call (`sdk/<version>`, `cli/<version>`). It only feeds the dashboard's Integrations status lines and changes nothing about the request. The SDK and CLI send it for you.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day of the window, YYYY-MM-DD, read in timezone. Default: 29 days before to.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day of the window, inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD, read in timezone. Default: today (29 days after from when only from is set); a later day is clamped to today.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: 7d, 30d, 90d, 12m (same date a year back, 366 days across a 29 February) or all (since the Team was created). Not with from or to.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Groups daily: day, week (from Monday), month, or auto (day to 90 days, week to 366, month beyond). Default: auto with range, day with from/to.

parameters.name: timezone
parameters.description: IANA zone the days are read in, e.g. Europe/Berlin. Default: UTC.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: Only these accounts (acc_...). Default: every account you can see. Repeat the key, comma-separate or mix; empties ignored.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Only Enrollments pinned to this Sequence version count; step rows follow its document order. Default: every version.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: motion, unibox (the Unibox), api (any API key or MCP grant), direct (unibox and api). Default: all. Repeat the key, comma-separate or mix; empties ignored.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Sections: performance, daily, steps, variants, paths, accounts, flags. Omitted: the summary. Repeat the key, comma-separate or mix; empties ignored.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Dotted paths kept in the sections, e.g. performance.reply.rate. A requested path always appears. Repeat the key, comma-separate or mix; empties ignored.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Orders lists: sent, acceptance.rate, reply.rate, inmail_reply.rate, last_activity_at, name. -key: desc. Repeat the key, comma-separate or mix; empties ignored.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per list section (motions, accounts), 1-100. Default: 5 in the summary, else every item.

parameters.name: compare
parameters.description: previous_period: each rate gains previous (the same number of days just before from) and delta (rate - previous rate).

200.description: One Motion's results, with a row per step (current version first, then steps only older versions have) and per variant. Each Contact counts once per Account. paths splits the Motion by the Contact's relationship to the account when the Enrollment started (provisional). Lags as for the overview. Grammar: include picks the sections (performance is totals under its section name), fields keeps dotted paths, sort and limit order and cut motions and accounts, compare=previous_period adds previous and delta to every rate, flags lists what to look at, and every Motion, account and step row carries next, the exact CLI call. Once any of these is given and include is not, the body is the summary: performance, the lists' top 5 by sent, flags. With none of them the full body of before is returned with a Deprecation header; it becomes the summary later. Here the summary is performance, accounts and flags; steps and variants come with include (steps alone leaves out each step's variants).

400.description: INVALID_REQUEST: an unknown query parameter, a malformed date (message starts from: or to:), from after to or a custom window over 3650 days (from:), range together with from or to (range:), an unknown range, bucket or origin, origin linkedin (never counted), or an unknown zone (timezone:). The grammar: a section this read does not have (include:), a path that is not a field or lies outside the returned sections (fields:), an unknown sort key (sort:), a limit outside 1 to 100 (limit:), a compare other than previous_period (compare:). TEAM_REQUIRED: an All-Teams key sent no X-Curviate-Team header (on an account route: with an account id that is not one); GET /v1/teams lists your teams.

value.message: A parameter failed validation.
Name the Team with the X-Curviate-Team header. GET /v1/teams lists yours.
Missing or invalid API key.

403.description: Only with account_id, in a team. ACCOUNT_NOT_SHARED: the teammate turned team access off for the account, so only they read its numbers. Not fixed by retrying.

value.message: The targeted account is not on an active seat.

404.description: RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND: no such Motion, or no such Sequence version. ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND: account_id is not one of your accounts, or was removed.

value.message: The referenced resource does not exist for this tenant.

429.description: Rate limited, slow down and retry after the hinted delay.

value.message: The per-account request rate limit was exceeded; retry after the delay in retry_hint. Per-team breaches carry RATE_LIMIT_TENANT; ingress-wide breaches (pre-auth, no per-client key) and upstream saturation both carry PLATFORM_RATE_LIMIT. A 429 on a budgeted action can also be BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, which is Curviate's own account-safety ceiling rather than a request-rate limit: it never reached LinkedIn, spent nothing, and carries row, reset_at and hint.

get.description: One Motion's results with a row per step and per variant: queued, executed, skipped, failed, then and else counts, and each messaging step's rate. Variants in document order, never ranked. The overview's include, fields, compare and flags apply. Read-only, no LinkedIn call.

parameters.name: X-Curviate-Team
parameters.description: The team id to act in (GET /v1/teams lists yours). Required with an All-Teams key, except on account routes. A team key accepts only its own team.

parameters.name: Curviate-Client
parameters.description: Informational: which Curviate client sent the call (`sdk/<version>`, `cli/<version>`). It only feeds the dashboard's Integrations status lines and changes nothing about the request. The SDK and CLI send it for you.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day of the window, YYYY-MM-DD, read in timezone. Default: 29 days before to.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day of the window, inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD, read in timezone. Default: today (29 days after from when only from is set); a later day is clamped to today.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: 7d, 30d, 90d, 12m (same date a year back, 366 days across a 29 February) or all (since the Team was created). Not with from or to.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Groups daily: day, week (from Monday), month, or auto (day to 90 days, week to 366, month beyond). Default: auto with range, day with from/to.

parameters.name: timezone
parameters.description: IANA zone the days are read in, e.g. Europe/Berlin. Default: UTC.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: Only these accounts (acc_...). Default: every account you can see. Repeat the key, comma-separate or mix; empties ignored.

200.description: Core activity in budget units for the accounts you may operate (yours; an Owner or Manager also the team's shared accounts). Every budgeted LinkedIn call counts, reads and Motion steps included. Each budget row counts its own unit, so figures are per row and never added across rows. quotas is exactly the quotas array of GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}: the current budget window, not the requested one.

account_id.description: The account filter when exactly one account is named; null otherwise (read account_ids).

account_ids.description: The account_id filter; [] when every visible account counts.

motion_ids.description: The motion_id filter of the overview; [] when every Motion counts.

origin.description: The origins counted (direct is unibox and api); null for every origin.

timezone.description: IANA zone the days are read in.

bucket.description: How daily is grouped (auto resolved: day up to 90 days, week up to 366, month beyond).

generated_at.description: UTC instant of the read; outcomes so far and maturing are measured at it.

budget_row.description: The budget row. Units differ per row: connection_requests_with_note, one invitation sent with a note; connection_requests_no_note, one invitation sent without a note; messages_first_degree, one message to a 1st-degree connection; inmail, one InMail sent; open_profile_inmail, one free message to an Open Profile; profile_views, one profile read; search, one search result line, not one query; comments, one comment posted; post_likes, one reaction to a post, a comment or a message; follows, one follow; content_poll, one content read: a page of posts, a feed, a company page or its followers; job_poll, one read of job postings; posts, one post published; endorsements, one skill endorsed; invite_responses, one received invitation accepted or declined; withdrawal_sweep, one sent invitation withdrawn; connections_sync, one background read of the connection list; inbox_sync, one background read of the inbox; profile_snapshot, one attempt of the daily Account snapshot.

failed.description: Of used, units of calls that failed.

refused.description: Calls refused before reaching LinkedIn: a ceiling, the activity window or a platform pause. Count of calls, not units.

daily.description: One entry per day of the window, oldest first, zeros included. used holds each budget row of types, never a total.

quotas.description: The account's quotas[], exactly as GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} serves it: the current budget window.

budget_row.description: The safety row. `search` counts result LINES, not queries issued; `content_poll` also debits `profile_views`. Two rows are not counters and say so in `kind`: `total_actions` is a tally of everything this account did in the window, and `pending_invites` is the outstanding invitation backlog read from the platform rather than something this account spends.

kind.description: Which arithmetic produced `used`. `debit`: actions this account spent, counted as they happen. `tally`: a sum across the debit rows in the window, which is why it has a warn threshold and no ceiling. `gauge`: a level read from the platform rather than counted here, so it falls on its own as invitations are accepted or withdrawn.

window.description: Calendar grain this row is counted in. UTC, not account-local. `null` on the gauge, which has no window at all.

window_start.description: ISO-8601 UTC start of the current window; `null` on the gauge.

resets_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant the current window rolls over and `used` returns to 0. `null` on the gauge: a backlog falls when invitations are accepted or withdrawn, not at a window edge, so naming an instant would promise something nothing keeps.

used.description: Where the account stands: actions counted in the current window for a debit row, the summed tally for `total_actions`, the observed backlog for the gauge. A debit row with no activity reports 0, never null. Only the gauge can be `null`, and only before anything has observed it: 0 there would be a backlog nobody looked at.

ceiling.description: What this account is allowed on this row in this window, as configured. `null` where the row deliberately has no ceiling: the tally is reported and never enforced, and an uncalibrated row has no figure at all. Change it on the safety policy; Curviate never clamps what you set.

effective_ceiling.description: What this row is ACTUALLY held to right now: `ceiling` with the account's warm-up ramp applied. Compare `used` against THIS one, and `band` is computed against it too. While warm-up holds an account back (its first four weeks after connect, after a quiet spell, or while it recovers from a restriction) the two differ, and in the first week after connect they differ by a factor of about seven. Equal to `ceiling` once the ramp is over, and `null` wherever `ceiling` is null. The account's ramp, its factor and the triggers behind it are on GET /v1/{account_id}/safety-policy as `warm_up`.

interface_ceiling.description: What a call through the matching ELEVATED interface is held to on this row: the `/v1/{account_id}/sales-navigator/...` and `/v1/{account_id}/recruiter/...` operations. Null when this row and limit profile have no such figure, which is every row on `basic` and `premium` and most rows everywhere. Everything else on this row (`ceiling`, `effective_ceiling`, `band` and `over_default`) is the STANDARD-interface figure, because one counter serves both interfaces and the standard side is the conservative one to band against. The consequence is worth reading: on a `sales_navigator` or `recruiter` account a row can report `band: "over"` while a call through the elevated interface still succeeds; the refusal the band predicts is the one a standard call gets.

remaining.description: `effective_ceiling` minus `used`, never below 0: what this account can still do on this row in the current window. Null when the row has no ceiling (`total_actions`) or no level yet (`pending_invites` before it was read).

effective_interface_ceiling.description: `interface_ceiling` with the account's warm-up ramp applied, and null wherever `interface_ceiling` is null. Read THIS to know where an elevated-interface call stops, for the same reason `effective_ceiling` rather than `ceiling` answers that for a standard one.

band.description: Where `used` sits against this row's own bands. `green` routine, `amber` at or past the routine band, `hard` at or past the warn-louder band, `over` at or past the ceiling, where the action is refused: limits are always enforced. A row with no figures reports `green` at every value, because there is nothing to be past.

over_default.description: Whether something on this row is configured above Curviate's own default. The safety policy carries the detail: which field, the value, the default and how well calibrated that default is.

halt.description: An active pause on this row because the platform refused a recent request on it, or `null`. A halt is not a ceiling: no limit you raise lifts it, and it clears itself when it expires. To lift one before it expires, send this row in `clear_halts` on `PATCH /v1/{account_id}/safety-policy`; that is recorded, and the pause returns if the platform refuses the account again.

reason.description: What the platform did: `rate_limited`, `platform_fault`, or `resend_cooldown` (the same invitation was sent too recently).

retry_after_seconds.description: Whole seconds until the pause expires.

observed_at.description: When the gauge's level was read from the platform. `null` on every other row, whose numbers are read live from Curviate's own records. Read it before acting on the backlog: the level is refreshed in the background, so it can be up to an hour old.

source.description: How well calibrated this row is, in descending order of trust: `substrate` (the transport layer's own guidance), `linkedin_official` (platform-published; reliable for mechanics such as credit counts and reset dates, not for safe volume), `practitioner` (corroborated operator experience), `inferred` (Curviate's own reasoning; flagged, never hidden), `unseeded` (no figure at all for this row on this account's limit profile, reported so nothing is silently missing, never presented as a number).
